The Achilles tendon is the strongest tendon in the human body.
Tennis elbow often also occurs in people who never play tennis.

teile.einleitung: The Viennese Classical period is an era of music in the late 18th and early 19th centuries. Its three great composers, Joseph Haydn, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart and Ludwig van Beethoven, all worked in Vienna. Their works are still among the most frequently played pieces of classical music today.
wichtigste: The Viennese Classical period lasted from about 1770 to 1827.
Its main representatives are Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven.
Joseph Haydn is often called the “father of the symphony”.
A classical symphony usually has four movements.
The first movement is usually in sonata form.
A string quartet consists of two violins, viola and cello.
The fortepiano replaced the harpsichord.

abschnitte.text: The **Viennese Classical period** covers roughly the time from 1770 to Beethoven's death in 1827. At that time Vienna was the capital of the Habsburg Empire and one of the most important music cities in Europe. Nobles, emperors and wealthy citizens supported musicians and organised concerts. Before the Classical period came the Baroque, with composers such as Johann Sebastian Bach, and after it came Romanticism.

**Joseph Haydn** (1732 to 1809) worked for almost 30 years for the princely Esterházy family. **Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart** (1756 to 1791) was a child prodigy from Salzburg and wrote over 600 works. **Ludwig van Beethoven** (1770 to 1827) came from Bonn to Vienna and went on composing even when he became deaf. The three knew each other: Mozart and Haydn were friends, and Beethoven took lessons from Haydn.

Classical music sounds clear, balanced and well structured. The melody is in the foreground, and the accompaniment is simpler than in the Baroque. **Sonata form**, with three sections, became especially important: exposition, development and recapitulation. Instead of the harpsichord, the **fortepiano** won out, a forerunner of today's piano, on which you could play loudly and softly.

The **symphony** is a large work for orchestra, usually in four movements. According to the usual numbering of the Hoboken catalogue, Haydn wrote 104 symphonies. In the finale of his 9th Symphony Beethoven set Friedrich Schiller's poem “Ode to Joy” to music. The **string quartet** with two violins, viola and cello was also popular, a form that Haydn strongly shaped.

So that the many works can be found, they were numbered in catalogues. Mozart's works are listed in the **Köchel catalogue**, abbreviated K. or KV, Haydn's in the Hoboken catalogue. The works of the Viennese Classical period are still played all over the world today, including in Swiss concert halls such as the Tonhalle in Zurich. The melody from Beethoven's 9th Symphony is today the anthem of the European Union.

begriffe.erklaerung: A period of time with typical features, for example in music.
A large musical work for orchestra, usually with four movements.
A self-contained part of a larger musical work.
A group of four string players: two violins, viola and cello.
An early piano in which small hammers strike the strings.

gewusst: Beethoven composed his 9th Symphony when he was already almost completely deaf.
Haydn's Symphony No. 94 is called the “Surprise Symphony” because a sudden loud beat interrupts the quiet music.
None of the three Viennese Classical composers came from Vienna; they all moved there later.

teile.einleitung: Sports politics includes all the decisions by states and federations that affect sport. This includes how the state promotes sport, but also how sport is used for political aims. Big sporting events such as the Olympic Games have often been the scene of boycotts and protests.
wichtigste: In 1980 the USA and many other states boycotted the Olympic Games in Moscow.
The reason was the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan.
In 1971 the rapprochement between the USA and China began with table tennis.
South Africa returned to the Olympic Summer Games in Barcelona in 1992.
The Federal Office of Sport FOSPO has its headquarters in Magglingen.
Youth and Sport supports children and young people aged 5 to 20.
Article 68 of the Federal Constitution regulates the Confederation's promotion of sport.

abschnitte.text: Article 68 of the **Federal Constitution** gives the Confederation the task of promoting sport. The responsible body is the **Federal Office of Sport** FOSPO, with its headquarters in Magglingen above Biel. There is also a university of sport and training facilities for top athletes there. The most important programme is **Youth and Sport**, which supports children and young people aged 5 to 20 in clubs and camps. The cantons and municipalities look after things such as gyms and school sport.

After the **Soviet invasion of Afghanistan** at the end of 1979, the USA and many other states boycotted the 1980 Olympic Games in Moscow. Switzerland took part in these Games. In 1984 the Soviet Union and many Eastern Bloc countries then boycotted the Games in Los Angeles. Only **Romania** took part anyway and won many medals.

Sport can also bring countries closer together. In 1971 an American table tennis team was invited to China; this is called **ping-pong diplomacy**. After that, relations between the USA and the People's Republic of China improved. Because of racial segregation, **apartheid**, South Africa was excluded from the Olympics for a long time and returned in Barcelona in 1992.

In Mexico City in 1968 the US sprinters **Tommie Smith** and **John Carlos** protested against racism on the winners' podium with raised fists. They were expelled from the Games for this, but today many people see them as role models. In 1969 the so-called Football War broke out between El Salvador and Honduras around World Cup qualifying matches. Its real causes, however, were disputes over land and immigration.

The **Olympic Charter** contains the basic rules of the Olympic Movement. Its Rule 50 forbids political demonstrations at Olympic sites. This is often debated, because athletes also want to express their opinions. Because the IOC, FIFA and many other federations are based in Switzerland, Switzerland plays a special role in international sports politics.

begriffe.erklaerung: Deliberately staying away in order to protest against something.
The former state racial segregation in South Africa.
The Swiss Federal Office of Sport in Magglingen (in German BASPO).
The basic rules of the Olympic Games and the IOC.

gewusst: More than 60 countries were missing from the 1980 Games in Moscow.
Since 1972 millions of Swiss children have taken part in Youth and Sport activities.
Ping-pong diplomacy began with a chance meeting of table tennis players at the 1971 World Championships in Japan.

teile.einleitung: A film character is a person, an animal or a creature that appears in a film and carries the story. Some film characters are so popular that they are known all over the world, such as Shrek, the Minions or Paddington. They make us laugh, cry and feel tense with excitement.
wichtigste: Film characters can be people, animals, robots, vehicles or fantasy creatures.
Pinocchio is a wooden puppet whose nose grows longer when he lies.
Shrek is a green ogre, and the Minions are little yellow helpers.
Paddington Bear loves orange marmalade.
Mary Poppins flies through the air with an umbrella.
Many film characters originally come from books.
Peter Pan is the character who never wants to grow up.

abschnitte.text: A **film character** is someone who plays a part in a film. The most important character is called the **main character** or protagonist, and their opponent is called the antagonist. Characters can be played by actors, drawn or created on the computer. Good film characters have wishes, strengths and weaknesses, so that you feel for them. They often change in the course of the story.

Many film characters first appeared in books. **Pinocchio** comes from an Italian children's book by Carlo Collodi; Disney filmed the story in 1940. When the wooden puppet lies, his nose grows longer. **Paddington** Bear was invented by the Briton Michael Bond; he comes from Peru and loves orange marmalade. **Peter Pan**, who never wants to grow up and lives in Neverland, also comes from a play and a book by J. M. Barrie.

**Shrek** is a green ogre who really just wants to live in peace in his swamp; his film came out in 2001. The yellow **Minions** appeared in 2010 in the film “Despicable Me” and speak a funny made-up language. The little elephant **Dumbo** from the 1941 Disney film can fly with his huge ears. Remy the rat from “Ratatouille” cooks better in Paris than many humans. Characters like these show that outsiders can achieve great things too.

In Pixar films even machines become heroes. **WALL-E** is a little robot who clears up rubbish on an abandoned Earth. In “Cars” **Lightning McQueen** is an ambitious racing car who learns about friendship. **Mary Poppins** is a magical nanny who flies through the air with an umbrella; the film with Julie Andrews came out in 1964. Making things and animals talk is called **personification**.

For live-action films, actors who will play the character are chosen at a **casting**. For animated films artists draw many designs until the appearance and the movements are right. **Voice actors** lend the characters their voices, and in the German version these are often different from those in the original. Today many characters are created on the computer and brought to life with motion capture. Costumes, make-up and music also help to make a character unmistakable.

You do not see popular film characters only at the cinema. They exist as cuddly toys, on school things, T-shirts and in video games; this is called **merchandising**. In theme parks such as Disneyland visitors meet their favourite characters in costume. Some characters get many sequels, and in this way whole film series come about. That is how characters such as Mickey Mouse have stayed famous for almost a hundred years.

begriffe.erklaerung: The most important character, around whom the story revolves.
The opponent of the main character.
A large, human-like creature from fairy tales.
A person who gives a character their voice, for example in another language.
Selling toys and other products featuring film characters.

gewusst: Paddington is named after Paddington station in London, where the Brown family finds him.
The Minions' language is a made-up language using words from many real languages.
In Italian, Pinocchio means roughly “pine nut”.

teile.einleitung: Football is the most popular sport in the world; millions of people play it or watch it. Two teams of eleven players each try to kick the ball into the opponents' goal. You may play the ball with any part of your body except your hands and arms; only the goalkeeper is an exception.
wichtigste: A team has eleven players on the pitch at the same time.
Only the goalkeeper may catch the ball with their hands inside the penalty area.
A normal adult match lasts 90 minutes.
Anyone shown the red card has to leave the pitch.
After a foul in the penalty area there is a penalty.
If the ball rolls over the touchline, there is a throw-in.
The men's World Cup takes place every 4 years.

abschnitte.text: Two teams of **eleven players** each play on a rectangular grass pitch. A match lasts two halves of 45 minutes each, so 90 minutes in total. The team that scores more goals wins. Besides the **goalkeeper** there are defenders, midfielders and strikers. The goalkeeper may catch the ball with their hands inside their penalty area.

The **referee** controls the match and blows the whistle for fouls. For serious fouls they show the yellow card as a caution or the **red card**, and then the player has to leave the pitch. A foul in the penalty area is punished with a **penalty**, a kick from the spot 11 metres away. If the ball rolls over the touchline, there is a throw-in; over the goal line, a corner kick or goal kick.

Ball games played with the feet already existed thousands of years ago, for example in China. Modern football developed in the 19th century in **England**, where the first football association was founded in 1863. English students and merchants also brought the game to Switzerland, which is why some clubs still have English names today, such as Grasshopper Club Zürich or Young Boys. The Swiss Football Association was founded in 1895.

The men's **football World Cup** takes place every four years, for the first time in Uruguay in 1930. The 2026 World Cup was held in the USA, Canada and Mexico. Women also have their own World Cup and European Championship. In 2025 the Women's European Championship took place in Switzerland. The world football federation **FIFA** has its headquarters in Zurich, and the European federation UEFA in Nyon.

The top men's league is called the **Super League**, and for women there is the Women's Super League. Below them, many leagues play, down to youth teams and amateur clubs. The Swiss Football Association has hundreds of thousands of registered players, which makes football the biggest team sport in the country. Well-known stadiums are the Wankdorf in Bern and St. Jakob-Park in Basel. In 1954 the men's World Cup took place in Switzerland.

begriffe.erklaerung: A penalty kick from 11 metres after a foul in the penalty area.
The large marked area in front of the goal.
A rule that stops a striker from waiting near the goal for the ball.
Throwing the ball back in with both hands after it has rolled over the touchline.
The top men's football league in Switzerland.

gewusst: A football weighs between 410 and 450 grams.
A professional player often runs 10 to 12 kilometres in one match.
FC Basel, FC Zürich and the Grasshoppers were all founded in the 19th century.

teile.einleitung: Copyright protects works such as books, music, films, photos, drawings and computer programs. It says that the person who created a work may decide how it is used. Anyone who shares music, posts pictures or copies texts should therefore know the most important rules.
wichtigste: In Switzerland copyright protection arises automatically as soon as a work is created.
Books, films and music are usually protected until 70 years after the author's death.
Computer programs are protected for 50 years after the author's death.
Works whose protection has expired are in the public domain and may be used freely.
Quoting is allowed if it serves to explain something and the source is given.
Offering protected films for download on the internet is not allowed, even privately.
Suisa looks after the rights of composers, lyricists and music publishers.

abschnitte.text: **Copyright** protects intellectual creations that have their own individual character. These include books, songs, films, paintings, photos, buildings and software. The **author** may decide whether and how the work is copied, distributed or changed. In Switzerland this is regulated by the Copyright Act, which was passed in 1992 and revised in 2020. You do not have to register the work anywhere; the protection arises automatically.

abschnitte.titel: How long does the protection last?
abschnitte.text: In Switzerland most works are protected until **70 years** after the author's death. For computer programs the period is 50 years. After that the works enter the **public domain**, and everyone may use them freely. That is why you can freely use pictures by Albert Anker or music by Mozart, for example. But watch out: a new recording of an old piece of music can still be protected.

For **personal use** you may use many things in Switzerland, for example copy a song for yourself. But offering protected films or music on the internet for others to download is forbidden. You may **quote** from a work if the quotation serves to explain something and the source is given. In the USA there is the flexible principle of **fair use**, which allows criticism or parody, for example. Anyone who puts other people's photos on a website without permission can receive an expensive bill.

Artists cannot check for themselves everywhere their works are played. **Collecting societies** do this for them. **Suisa** looks after music and collects fees, for example, from radio stations, concerts and restaurants. ProLitteris is responsible for texts and pictures, and Suissimage for films. The money is then distributed to the authors.

Some authors want their works to be shared freely. For this there are **Creative Commons licences**, which have been available since 2002. With the licence “CC BY” you may use the work but must always name the author. Under the principle of **copyleft**, adapted versions must also be passed on under the same free conditions. Wikipedia uses free licences like these for its texts and many pictures.

begriffe.erklaerung: The person who created a work.
No longer protected and free for everyone to use.
Permission to use a work under certain conditions.
An organisation that collects and distributes fees for authors.
Free works must stay free even when they are adapted.

gewusst: In Switzerland downloading music and films for personal use is allowed, but uploading them for others is not.
Since 2020 even quite ordinary photos have been protected in Switzerland, even if they have no special artistic character.
The © symbol is not necessary in Switzerland, because protection exists even without it.

teile.einleitung: Swimming means moving through water under your own power without sinking. It is one of the healthiest sports because almost all your muscles work while your joints are spared. If you can swim well, you are safer in the water and can rescue yourself.
wichtigste: The four swimming strokes are breaststroke, front crawl, backstroke and butterfly.
Front crawl is the fastest swimming stroke.
In breaststroke you move your arms and legs a bit like a frog.
The butterfly stroke is also called “fly”.
An Olympic swimming pool is 50 metres long.
In races the swimmers usually dive into the water from the starting block.
The SLRG teaches swimming safety rules, for example: never jump into unfamiliar water.

abschnitte.text: In **breaststroke** you kick your legs out like a frog and pull your arms back at the same time. In **front crawl** your legs kick quickly up and down, and your arms pull through the water one after the other. Front crawl is the fastest stroke, which is why almost everyone chooses it in freestyle. In backstroke you lie on your back. **Butterfly** is the most tiring stroke because both arms swing over the water at the same time.

An Olympic pool is 50 metres long; it is also called a **long-course pool**. There are races over distances from 50 to 1500 metres. The start is usually a dive from the **starting block**; only in backstroke do you start in the water. In the **medley relay** each team member swims a different stroke. The time is measured electronically with touch pads at the edge of the pool.

**Swimming goggles** protect your eyes from the chlorinated water and give you clear vision. A swimming cap keeps your hair together and makes you a little faster in competitions. For training there are aids such as kickboards and fins. The **chlorine** in the water kills germs and keeps the water clean.

The Swiss Lifesaving Society **SLRG** has drawn up simple **swimming safety rules**. One of them is: never jump into unfamiliar water, because it might not be deep enough or might hide stones. Children should never go into the water alone, and you do not swim with a full or completely empty stomach. In rivers and lakes the water is often colder and more dangerous than in an indoor pool. That is why many Swiss schools do the water safety check.

Switzerland has many lakes and rivers where you can swim in summer. In Basel **swimming in the Rhine** is very popular: you let yourself drift along with a waterproof bag. In Zurich and Bern there are old river baths, known as “Badis”. Noè Ponti from Ticino won Olympic bronze over 100 metres butterfly in Tokyo in 2021.

begriffe.erklaerung: A race in which you may choose any stroke; almost everyone swims front crawl.
A race in which you swim all four strokes one after the other.
A raised platform at the edge of the pool from which you dive into the water.
The Swiss Lifesaving Society, which trains lifeguards.

gewusst: The butterfly stroke developed from breaststroke when swimmers started bringing their arms forward over the water.
At the end of the pool top swimmers turn with a quick roll, the tumble turn.
A 50-metre pool often has room for ten lanes.

teile.einleitung: The Olympic Games are the largest sporting festival in the world. Every few years thousands of athletes from almost every country meet to compete for gold, silver and bronze in many sports. There are Summer Games and Winter Games, and their history goes back to ancient Greece.
wichtigste: The ancient Olympic Games took place in Greece.
Pierre de Coubertin is regarded as the founder of the modern Olympic Games.
The first Games of modern times took place in Athens in 1896.
The Olympic flag shows five rings.
Gold is awarded for first place, silver for second and bronze for third.
There are normally four years between two Summer Games.
The IOC has its headquarters in Lausanne, and St Moritz has hosted the Games twice.

abschnitte.text: The first Olympic Games took place in the sacred site of **Olympia** in Greece. The year 776 BC is regarded as the beginning. The Games were held every four years in honour of the god Zeus. There were running races, wrestling, boxing and chariot races. The winners received a wreath of olive branches.

The Frenchman **Pierre de Coubertin** revived the Games and founded the International Olympic Committee in 1894. In 1896 the first Olympic Games of modern times took place in **Athens**. Since 1924 there have also been Olympic Winter Games. Since 1994 the Summer and Winter Games have alternated every two years, so that there are four years between two Summer Games. Straight after the Games come the Paralympics for people with disabilities.

The **Olympic rings** in blue, yellow, black, green and red stand for the five continents united by sport. The **Olympic flame** is lit in Olympia with a concave mirror and sunlight and brought to the host country in a torch relay. There it burns in the stadium throughout the Games. The motto is “faster, higher, stronger, together”.

The best athletes receive **medals**: gold for first place, silver for second and **bronze** for third. At the Summer Games there are over 300 events, for example in athletics, swimming, gymnastics or football. At the Winter Games athletes compete in skiing, ice hockey, bobsleigh or figure skating. The 2026 Winter Games took place in Italy, in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo.

The International Olympic Committee has had its headquarters in **Lausanne** since 1915, where you can also visit the Olympic Museum. **St Moritz** hosted the Olympic Winter Games in 1928 and 1948. In 2020 the Winter Youth Olympic Games took place in Lausanne. Swiss athletes win many medals, especially at the Winter Games, for example in alpine skiing.

begriffe.erklaerung: The International Olympic Committee, based in Lausanne.
The place in Greece where the ancient Games took place.
Olympic Games for athletes with disabilities.
The flame that is lit in Olympia and burns during the Games.
The time of ancient Greece and the Roman Empire.

gewusst: Today the gold medals are made mostly of silver and are only coated with gold.
At the ancient Games the athletes competed naked.
From 1912 to 1948 medals were also awarded for art at the Olympic Games, for example for painting and music.

teile.einleitung: Film production is all the work needed before a film is shown in the cinema or on screen. From the first idea through the screenplay and the shooting to the editing and the advertising, hundreds of people often work together. Each of them has a very particular task.
wichtigste: A film is made in several phases: preparation, shooting and post-production.
The screenplay contains the plot, the scenes and the dialogue.
The director leads the shooting and tells the actors how to act.
A storyboard uses sketches to show the planned shots.
The clapperboard helps to match picture and sound later.
A green screen is later replaced by another picture.
In editing, the best shots are put together into a film.
A trailer is a short advertising film with clips from the new film.

abschnitte.text: It all starts with an idea, from which a **screenplay** with plot, scenes and dialogue is written. The **producer** looks for money for the film and holds everything together. In pre-production, locations are found, costumes designed and a shooting schedule drawn up. A **storyboard** uses drawn sketches to show what each shot should look like. At the **casting** actors audition for the parts.

During the shoot the **director** leads the work and tells the actors how to act. The camera operator takes care of the picture, and the sound team of clean recordings of voices and noises. Before each take the **clapperboard** is snapped shut so that picture and sound match exactly later. A scene is often shot many times until everything is right. A single day of shooting sometimes produces only a few minutes of finished film.

At the filming location, the **set**, many specialists work together. Make-up artists do the actors' make-up, costume designers take care of the clothes, and the art department builds rooms and scenery. Dangerous scenes such as falls or chases are filmed by **stunt performers** instead of the actors. Lighting technicians set up spotlights so that the light is right. One person makes sure that clothes and objects stay the same from shot to shot; this is called continuity.

Many scenes are filmed in front of a **green screen**, a green wall. Later, on the computer, the green is replaced by another picture, for example a mountain landscape or outer space. In this way actors can seem to fly or stand on distant planets. Today whole characters, cities or explosions are created with **computer animation**. This work is called visual effects.

After the shoot, **post-production** begins. In **editing** the best shots are chosen and put together in the right order. After that music, noises and effects are added. For other countries, voice actors record the film again in another language; this is called **dubbing**. In Switzerland many films are also shown in the original language with subtitles in German and French.

Once the film is finished, it has to reach its audience. A **trailer** shows short, exciting clips and makes people curious. A **distributor** makes sure the film is shown in cinemas or on streaming services. Big Hollywood films often cost over a hundred million dollars, Swiss films usually only a few million francs. In Switzerland the Federal Office of Culture and regional foundations support many films with **film funding**.

begriffe.erklaerung: A sequence of sketches that shows the individual shots before filming.
The place where a film scene is shot.
A hinged board that is snapped shut before a take so that picture and sound match.
All the work after the shoot, such as editing, sound and effects.
Re-recording the voices of a film in another language.

gewusst: The credits of big films often contain several thousand names of people who worked on them.
Green is chosen for the green screen because this colour hardly appears in skin and hair.
The clapperboard shows the name of the film, the scene number and the take number.

teile.einleitung: Ada Lovelace was an English mathematician who lived in the 19th century. In 1843 she wrote an algorithm for Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine, which is regarded as the first computer program. In this she was more than a hundred years ahead of her time.
wichtigste: Ada Lovelace lived in England from 1815 to 1852.
She was the daughter of the famous poet Lord Byron.
Her mother encouraged her talent for mathematics from an early age.
She worked with the inventor Charles Babbage.
In 1843 she wrote an algorithm for the Analytical Engine, which is regarded as the first computer program.
She realised that calculating machines could also process music or pictures.
A programming language is named Ada in her honour.

abschnitte.text: Ada was born in London on 10 December 1815. Her father was the poet **Lord Byron**, who left the family shortly after her birth. Her mother, Annabella Milbanke, loved mathematics and had Ada taught by good teachers. She hoped mathematics would protect Ada from her father's wild imagination. Later Ada married a nobleman and so became the Countess of **Lovelace**.

At the age of 17 Ada met the inventor **Charles Babbage**. He had plans for mechanical calculating machines made of cogs and levers. His **Analytical Engine** was to be controlled with punched cards and could have done many things today's computers can do. But it was never built, because it was too expensive and complicated. Ada was thrilled by the ideas and stayed in contact with Babbage for a long time.

An Italian engineer wrote an article in French about Babbage's machine. In 1843 Ada translated it into English and added her own notes, which were three times as long as the text. In Note G she described step by step how the machine could calculate the so-called **Bernoulli numbers**. This **algorithm** is regarded as the first computer program in the world. That is why Ada is often called the first programmer.

Ada recognised something that even Babbage hardly saw. She wrote that such a machine could not only calculate with numbers but also process **symbols**. In this way it could, for example, compose music. Today computers do exactly that with pictures, music and text. Ada Lovelace died of cancer in 1852 at the age of only 36.

In the 1980s a programming language of the US Department of Defense was given the name **Ada**. Every year in October **Ada Lovelace Day** is celebrated to make women in science and technology more visible. In Switzerland, too, there are programmes that aim to get girls excited about computer science. Today Ada is regarded as a role model for women in technology.

begriffe.erklaerung: Exact step-by-step instructions for solving a task.
A mechanical calculating machine planned by Charles Babbage.
A card with holes used to give machines instructions.
A person who writes instructions for computers.

gewusst: Ada Lovelace called her way of thinking “poetical science”.
Her father Lord Byron died when she was only eight years old, and she had never really got to know him.
Part of Babbage's calculating machine was built only long after his death, following the old plans, and it worked.

teile.einleitung: **Swiss folk music** is as varied as the country itself. It includes yodelling, the alphorn, Ländler music and old customs such as coin swirling (Talerschwingen). Many traditions are handed down from generation to generation and kept alive at festivals.
wichtigste: Small groups that play traditional dance music are called Ländler bands.
The Zäuerli is a slow, wordless natural yodel from the Appenzell Hinterland.
In Talerschwingen you make a coin circle inside a clay bowl.
With the Betruf, Alpine herdsmen call through a milk funnel in the evening to ask for protection for the pasture and the cattle.
The Federal Yodelling Festival takes place every three years.
The “House of Folk Music” is in Altdorf.
“Le Ranz des vaches” is a herdsmen's song from the canton of Fribourg.

abschnitte.text: A **Ländler band** is a small group of musicians that plays traditional Swiss dance music. Typical instruments are the **Schwyzerörgeli**, clarinet, piano and double bass. They play dances such as the Ländler, schottische, waltz and polka. Ländler music sounds different depending on the region, for example in Central Switzerland, in the Appenzell region or in the Grisons.

In **yodelling** the voice switches quickly between chest voice and head voice. The **natural yodel** has no words and consists only of syllables. In the Appenzell Hinterland people sing the slow, solemn **Zäuerli**. At the **Federal Yodelling Festival**, which takes place **every three years**, yodellers, alphorn players and flag throwers from all over Switzerland meet.

The **alphorn** is a long wooden horn that herdsmen used in the past to communicate. The **Büchel** is related to the alphorn but shorter and coiled like a trumpet. In **Trychle** groups shake large forged bells, the **Treicheln**, in the same rhythm. In the Appenzell region there is **Talerschwingen**: a **coin** circles in a clay bowl and makes a humming sound to accompany the yodel.

On some Alpine pastures the herdsman calls the **Betruf** (evening prayer call) in the evening. He holds a wooden **milk funnel** in front of his mouth so that his voice carries far across the meadows. With the prayer he asks for protection for people, animals and the pasture during the night. This custom is widespread mainly in Catholic areas of central and eastern Switzerland.

abschnitte.titel: Ranz des vaches and the House of Folk Music
abschnitte.text: **“Le Ranz des vaches”** is a herdsmen's song in French from the canton of **Fribourg**. It is sung at the winegrowers' festival, the **Fête des Vignerons** in **Vevey**, and moves the audience every time. If you would like to learn more about folk music, you will find the **House of Folk Music** in **Altdorf** in the canton of Uri. It collects, researches and passes on the folk music of Switzerland.

gewusst: The Fête des Vignerons in Vevey takes place only a few times a century.
Yodelling exists not only in Switzerland but also in Austria, Bavaria and even among peoples in Africa.

teile.einleitung: The trumpet is a brass instrument with a bright, brilliant sound. You blow into a mouthpiece, and the vibrating lips make the air in the tube vibrate. You hear trumpets in the orchestra, in jazz, in brass bands and on festive occasions.
wichtigste: The trumpet is a brass instrument.
It is usually made of brass.
You blow into the mouthpiece, and your lips vibrate.
A normal trumpet has three valves.
The sound comes out of the wide bell.
Related instruments are the trombone, the horn and the tuba.
The tuba is the largest and lowest brass instrument in the orchestra.

abschnitte.text: A trumpet consists of a bent **tube** made of brass that is about one and a half metres long. So that the instrument stays handy, the tube is coiled several times. At the front is the **mouthpiece**, into which you blow. At the end the tube opens out into the **bell**, from which the sound comes. In the middle are three valves, which you press with the fingers of your right hand.

When playing the trumpet, the lips press lightly against the mouthpiece and **vibrate** when you blow air through. This vibration is passed on to the column of air in the tube. More or less lip tension produces higher or lower notes. If you press a **valve**, the air's path is lengthened by an extra piece of tube, and the note becomes lower. In this way you can play all the notes of a scale with only three valves.

Trumpet-like instruments already existed in ancient Egypt; two of them were found in the tomb of the pharaoh Tutankhamun. For a long time there was only the **natural trumpet** without valves, on which only a few notes could be played. In the Middle Ages and the Baroque period the trumpet was an instrument for kings, princes and celebrations. Valves were only invented in Germany in the early 19th century. Since then the trumpet can play all the notes and has become popular in many styles of music.

In a **symphony orchestra** there are usually two to four trumpets. Joseph Haydn wrote a famous trumpet concerto around 1796. In **jazz** the trumpeter Louis Armstrong from the USA became world-famous. In Switzerland many children and young people play the trumpet in a **music society** or brass band. With a mute in the bell you can make the sound quieter or muffled.

The trumpet has many relatives, all played with vibrating lips. Instead of valves the **trombone** has a slide that you push back and forth. The horn has a round, tightly coiled tube and a soft sound. The **tuba** is the largest and lowest brass instrument in the orchestra. The cornet and the flugelhorn look similar to the trumpet but sound a little softer.

begriffe.erklaerung: A wind instrument in which the note is made by lips vibrating against the mouthpiece.
A push button that lengthens the air's path and makes the note lower.
The small funnel against which you put your lips and blow.
The wide, open end from which the sound comes.
An insert for the bell that makes the sound quieter or different.

gewusst: If you unrolled the tube of a trumpet into a straight line, it would be about one and a half metres long, taller than most children.
What matters for a trumpet is not the material but the vibration of the lips, which is why even an alphorn made of wood counts as a brass instrument.
The trumpets from Tutankhamun's tomb are over 3000 years old.

teile.einleitung: Doping means that athletes use banned substances or methods to improve their performance. Doping is unfair to the others and can seriously harm your health. That is why there are strict rules and tests all over the world.
wichtigste: Doping is the use of banned substances or methods to improve performance.
The World Anti-Doping Agency WADA has its headquarters in Montreal.
The Festina affair at the 1998 Tour de France led to WADA being founded.
Since 2022 the foundation Swiss Sport Integrity has carried out the tests in Switzerland.
In 2012 Lance Armstrong was stripped of his seven Tour de France wins.
EPO doping makes the haematocrit value in the blood rise sharply.
In 1988 the sprinter Ben Johnson lost his Olympic gold medal because of doping.

abschnitte.text: Anything on WADA's **Prohibited List** counts as **doping**. This includes medicines such as anabolic steroids for more muscle, hormones such as **EPO** for more red blood cells, or stimulants. Banned methods count too, for example putting your own blood back into your body. The list is checked and updated every year.

Doping substances can have serious side effects. EPO makes the blood thicker, raises the **haematocrit** and can lead to blood clots and heart attacks. Anabolic steroids can damage the liver, the heart and the body's hormone balance. Doping is especially dangerous for teenagers, whose bodies are still developing.

Doping tests take place at competitions and also unannounced during training. Urine and blood are examined in a laboratory. Top athletes in the testing pool must say where they are and name a 60-minute time slot each day for testing. For testosterone doping, for example, the ratio of testosterone to epitestosterone in the urine is checked. In Switzerland the foundation **Swiss Sport Integrity** in Bern has been responsible for this since 2022.

In 1988 the Canadian sprinter **Ben Johnson** lost his 100-metre gold medal in Seoul because the substance stanozolol was found. At the 1998 Tour de France large amounts of doping substances were discovered at the Festina team: the **Festina affair**. In 2012 the professional cyclist Lance Armstrong was stripped of all seven of his Tour wins. In East Germany there was a state-run doping programme called State Plan Topic 14.25.

After the Festina affair the **World Anti-Doping Agency WADA** was founded in Lausanne in 1999. Today its headquarters are in Montreal in Canada. In 2016 the Canadian lawyer Richard McLaren presented a report for WADA on state-organised doping in Russia. Anyone who has doped is banned, has to give back medals and often loses their sponsors.

begriffe.erklaerung: The World Anti-Doping Agency, which fights doping around the world.
A hormone that stimulates the production of red blood cells and is misused as a doping substance.
The proportion of blood cells in the blood; it rises with EPO doping.
The list of all substances and methods that are banned in sport.
A punishment in which an athlete may not take part in competitions for a period of time.

gewusst: Some cold medicines can also contain banned substances, so athletes have to be very careful.
Samples are often stored for years and tested again later with new methods.
The word doping probably comes from “dop”, an intoxicating drink from South Africa.

teile.einleitung: Jugend+Sport (Youth and Sport), J+S for short, is the Confederation's sports promotion programme for children and young people. It supports clubs, schools and camps with money and trains the leaders. This means that a great many young people in Switzerland can do sport cheaply.
wichtigste: Youth and Sport is a programme of the Confederation and is carried out together with the cantons.
It is run by the Federal Office of Sport (FOSPO), which is part of the DDPS.
In the 1970s J+S replaced military pre-training.
Leaders need J+S leader training.
FOSPO runs a national youth sports centre in Tenero in Ticino.

abschnitte.text: **Jugend+Sport** is the sports promotion programme of the **Confederation**. It is the responsibility of the **Federal Office of Sport**, known in German as **BASPO**, based in Magglingen. FOSPO belongs to the Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport, abbreviated **DDPS** (in German VBS). The **cantons** help to carry it out. Children and young people aged from about 5 to 20 can take part.

Before J+S there was **military pre-training**. It was aimed at young men and was meant to prepare them for military service. In the **1970s** it was replaced by Youth and Sport. The new programme was open to **girls and boys** from the very start. Since then the focus has been on the joy of exercise and on health.

Anyone who leads J+S courses needs **leader training** in the sport concerned. This ensures the quality of the courses. The Confederation pays **contributions** towards courses and camps run by clubs and schools. This makes sports activities cheaper for children. Many sports are supported, from football and swimming to camp sports and hiking.

In **Tenero** on Lake Maggiore, FOSPO runs the **Centro Sportivo Nazionale della Gioventù** (National Youth Sports Centre). Many sports camps for school classes and clubs take place there. There are sports grounds, halls and opportunities for water sports. In **Magglingen** above Biel is the Swiss Federal Institute of Sport. Sports teachers and coaches are also trained there.

gewusst: Many scout and youth group camps are supported as J+S camps.
The word sport is even part of the name of a federal department, the DDPS.

teile.einleitung: The Breitling Orbiter 3 was a balloon in which the Swiss Bertrand Piccard and the Briton Brian Jones became the first to fly round the whole world without landing, in 1999. The journey began in the village of Château-d’Oex in the canton of Vaud and lasted almost 20 days. With it they achieved one of the last great records in aviation.
wichtigste: The Breitling Orbiter 3 took off on 1 March 1999 in Château-d’Oex.
On board were Bertrand Piccard and Brian Jones.
It was the first round-the-world balloon flight without landing.
The flight lasted almost 20 days.
The balloonists covered over 40,000 kilometres.
They landed in the desert in Egypt on 21 March 1999.
The capsule is now in a museum in the USA.

abschnitte.text: The Breitling Orbiter 3 was a so-called **Rozière balloon**. It combined a chamber of helium with one of hot air, heated with propane gas. When inflated it was about 55 metres tall. Below it hung a **pressurised cabin** in which the two pilots lived, slept and worked.

**Bertrand Piccard** is a doctor and adventurer from Lausanne. His grandfather Auguste Piccard was the first to fly into the stratosphere in 1931, and his father Jacques Piccard dived to the deepest point of the ocean in 1960. His partner was the British balloonist **Brian Jones**. Two earlier attempts with the balloons Orbiter 1 and 2 had failed.

On 1 March 1999 the balloon took off in **Château-d’Oex** in the canton of Vaud. The pilots used the strong high-altitude winds, the so-called **jet stream**, to travel east quickly. They crossed Africa, Asia, the Pacific and the Atlantic. Towards the end the gas ran low, and they had to plan very carefully.

On 21 March 1999 Piccard and Jones landed in the desert in **Egypt**. They had covered more than 40,000 kilometres. The journey lasted 19 days, 21 hours and 47 minutes. They had already crossed the finishing line over Mauritania before that, setting the **world record**.

The capsule of the Breitling Orbiter 3 is now on display in the National Air and Space Museum in the USA. Bertrand Piccard used his fame to campaign for clean energy. With the solar aeroplane **Solar Impulse**, he and André Borschberg flew round the Earth in 2015 and 2016 using only solar energy. A well-known international **balloon week** takes place in Château-d’Oex every year.

begriffe.erklaerung: A balloon that combines gas and hot air.
A very strong wind high up that blows round the Earth.
A closed cabin in which you can breathe even at great heights.
A journey all the way round the Earth.

gewusst: The name Breitling comes from a Swiss watch company that supported the project.
By profession Bertrand Piccard is a psychiatrist and has studied hypnosis a great deal.

teile.einleitung: A job or profession is work that you have learnt and with which you earn money. The baker bakes fresh bread every morning, the postman brings letters and parcels, and the doctor helps sick people. In Switzerland there are hundreds of different jobs, and many of them are learnt through an apprenticeship.
wichtigste: A job is learnt work with which you earn your living.
The baker bakes bread, often in the middle of the night.
The postman brings letters and parcels to your home.
In Switzerland about two thirds of young people do a vocational apprenticeship.
In an apprenticeship you learn at the company and at vocational school.
There are around 250 different apprenticeship trades in Switzerland.
In a taster apprenticeship you can try out a job.

abschnitte.text: A **job** is work for which you need special knowledge and skills. With their wages people pay for their home, food and clothes. Jobs can be divided into groups, such as crafts, health, technology, trade or education. Many people also change their job at some point in their lives.

The **baker** often starts as early as 3 or 4 o’clock in the morning so that the bread is fresh for breakfast. The **postman**, or Pöstler as people say in Switzerland, delivers letters and parcels in every neighbourhood. We also meet the bus driver, the hairdresser and the shop assistant almost every day. Without them our everyday life would not work.

In Switzerland the **vocational apprenticeship** is very popular. You work three to four days a week at a training company and go to vocational school for one to two days. This is called the **dual vocational training system**. At the end you receive a Federal VET Diploma, EFZ for short, or after a two-year apprenticeship a Federal VET Certificate, EBA for short.

From about the seventh year at school, pupils start thinking about **choosing a career**. In a **taster apprenticeship** you spend a few days at a company and see whether you like the work. At the careers advice service, experts help you find out your own strengths and interests. If you want to keep learning after the apprenticeship, you can take the vocational baccalaureate and later go to a university of applied sciences.

Jobs change with technology. In the past there were many coachmen and blacksmiths; today we need IT specialists, media technologists and experts for solar panels instead. Some jobs almost disappear completely, others are newly created. That is why it is important to keep learning new things all your life.

begriffe.erklaerung: Training at a company and at vocational school.
Federal VET Diploma, the qualification at the end of a three or four-year apprenticeship.
A few days in which you try out a job (German “Schnupperlehre”).
The money you get for your work.

gewusst: The German word for job, “Beruf”, comes from “berufen”, to call, so people felt called to a particular kind of work.
Swiss apprentices regularly win many medals at the WorldSkills championships.

teile.einleitung: In a motion problem you work out when and where vehicles, runners or other things that move at a certain speed meet. Problems like these are a classic in maths lessons. With the simple formula distance equals speed times time, many tricky puzzles can be solved.
wichtigste: Motion problems connect distance, speed and time.
The most important formula is: distance equals speed times time.
In a chase, you work with the difference between the speeds.
When two things meet head on, you add the speeds together.
If train A leaves at 8 o’clock at 80 km/h and train B at 9 o’clock at 120 km/h, B catches up with it at 11 o’clock.
A sketch or a distance-time graph helps you to solve it.
All the data must be in matching units.

abschnitte.text: A **motion problem** describes a situation in which something moves at a constant speed. Usually you are looking for a point in time, a distance or a speed. The basic formula is **s = v · t**, distance equals speed times time. From this it also follows that time equals distance divided by speed.

Train A leaves at 8 o’clock at 80 km/h, and train B follows at 9 o’clock from the same station at 120 km/h. At 9 o’clock train A already has a **head start** of 80 kilometres. Train B is 40 kilometres per hour faster, so it catches up 40 kilometres each hour. It needs 2 hours for 80 kilometres, so it catches up with A at **11 o’clock**.

At 11 o’clock train A has been travelling for 3 hours and has covered 3 times 80, which is 240 kilometres. Train B has been travelling for 2 hours and covers 2 times 120, which is also 240 kilometres. Both are at the same place, so the solution is right. You should do a **check** like this with every problem.

If two vehicles drive **towards each other**, the gap between them shrinks by the sum of their speeds. If Zurich and Bern are about 120 kilometres apart and two cars drive towards each other at 70 and 50 km/h, they meet after one hour. In a **distance-time graph** you draw each movement as a line, and the point where they cross shows the meeting. That way you can see the solution even without calculating.

Often speeds are given in km/h and distances in metres. Then you first have to convert: 1 metre per second is **3.6 km/h**. So a cyclist going at 18 km/h travels 5 metres per second. If you work carefully with **units**, you make fewer mistakes.

begriffe.erklaerung: How much distance you cover in a certain time.
The distance someone is already ahead.
A drawing that shows where someone is at what time.
Working it through again to see whether the solution is really right.

gewusst: Railway timetables are planned with graphical timetables, which are large distance-time graphs.
In ancient Greece there was already a famous puzzle in which swift Achilles chases a tortoise.

teile.einleitung: 51 Pegasi b is a planet that orbits a star other than our Sun. In 1995 it was the first such planet to be discovered around a Sun-like star. It was found by the Geneva astronomers Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz.
wichtigste: 51 Pegasi b is an exoplanet, that is a planet outside our solar system.
Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz from Geneva discovered it in 1995.
It orbits the star 51 Pegasi in the constellation of Pegasus.
The star is about 50 light years from Earth.
The planet needs only about 4.2 days for one orbit.
It is a hot gas giant, a so-called hot Jupiter.
In 2019 Mayor and Queloz received the Nobel Prize in Physics for the discovery.

abschnitte.text: Michel Mayor and his doctoral student **Didier Queloz** from the University of Geneva observed the star 51 Pegasi at the Haute-Provence Observatory in southern France. In October 1995 they announced that a planet was orbiting this star. It was the first **exoplanet** found around a Sun-like star. Before that, planets were known only around a pulsar, a very special remnant of a star. The discovery was a sensation in astronomy.

The planet itself could not be seen because the star outshines it far too much. Instead the researchers used the **radial velocity method**. A planet pulls on its star with its gravity, so that the star wobbles slightly back and forth. This wobble changes the colour of the starlight by a tiny amount. With a very precise instrument, a **spectrograph**, Mayor and Queloz were able to measure it.

51 Pegasi b is a **gas giant** with about half the mass of Jupiter. But it orbits much closer to its star than Mercury does to the Sun. It needs only about 4.2 days for one orbit. That is why it is very hot, estimated at over 1000 degrees Celsius. Planets like this are called **hot Jupiters**, and before they were discovered they were thought to be impossible.

The star 51 Pegasi lies in the **constellation of Pegasus** and is about 50 light years away from us. On a very dark night you can just see it with the naked eye. In 2015 the public was allowed to suggest names for exoplanets. Since then the planet has also officially been called **Dimidium**, which is Latin for “half”. The name recalls its mass of about half a Jupiter.

The discovery showed that other stars have planets too. Since then more than 5000 exoplanets have been found (as of 2025). In 2019 Mayor and Queloz received the **Nobel Prize in Physics** for this. The University of Geneva and the University of Bern are still leaders in exoplanet research today. Switzerland built, for example, the space telescope **CHEOPS**, which has been studying exoplanets since 2019.

begriffe.erklaerung: A planet that orbits a star other than the Sun.
The distance light travels in a year, about 9.5 trillion kilometres.
A large gas planet that orbits very close to its star.
An instrument that splits light into its colours and measures it precisely.

gewusst: A year on 51 Pegasi b lasts only just over four Earth days.
Mayor and Queloz shared the 2019 Nobel Prize with the Canadian-American cosmologist James Peebles.
At first many astronomers did not believe the discovery, because such a hot giant planet did not fit the theories of the time.

teile.einleitung: Before sport you prepare your body for exercise by warming up. In this way your muscles, heart and joints slowly get going. This protects you from injuries and helps you perform better.
wichtigste: You warm up before sport, at the start of the PE lesson.
When you warm up, your muscles become warm and supple.
Your heartbeat gets faster and the blood flows more quickly through your body.
A good warm-up helps to prevent injuries.
You start easily and slowly and then build up.
A normal warm-up lasts about 10 to 20 minutes.

abschnitte.text: When you warm up, you move more than when you are resting. That is why your **heart** beats faster and pumps more blood through your body. More blood flows to your **muscles**, and they become warm and more stretchy. Your body produces heat, which is why you feel warm afterwards and perhaps sweat a little. Your joints also become more mobile.

Warm muscles and joints are better prepared for the strain. This means you are less likely to get injured, for example with a **pulled muscle**. You also react faster and can achieve more. Your mind gets ready for the sport too. That is why warming up belongs in every PE lesson and every training session.

You start **easily and slowly**, for example with light jogging. Then the pace is gradually increased. This is often followed by **running drills** with exercises such as high knees, heel flicks or skipping. They warm you up and train your running technique at the same time. At the end, exercises that already belong to the sport are a good fit, such as passing in football.

A normal warm-up lasts about **10 to 20 minutes**. Longer would not be good, because otherwise you would already get tired. In cold weather the body needs a little more time. After sport you often **cool down** with some easy jogging. This lets the body recover slowly and the pulse goes down again.

gewusst: Top athletes often warm up for longer before a competition than is usual at school.
Musicians and singers warm up too, for example their fingers or their voice.

teile.einleitung: The history of video games begins in the 1950s and 1960s with simple experiments on computers and stretches to today's huge game worlds. Games such as Pong, Pac-Man, Tetris and Super Mario have shaped generations. Today video games are one of the most important entertainment media in the world.
wichtigste: Early computer games were made at universities in the 1950s and 1960s.
In 1972 the first home console, the Magnavox Odyssey, and the table tennis game “Pong” came out.
In amusement arcades people played on coin-operated arcade machines.
Pac-Man is chased through his maze by ghosts.
Shigeru Miyamoto invented Mario and Link; Mario was originally a plumber.
Tetris was invented in the Soviet Union in 1984.
In 1989 Nintendo brought out the portable Game Boy.
Minecraft comes from Sweden.

abschnitte.text: As early as 1958 the physicist William Higinbotham built a simple tennis game on a measuring instrument, which became known as “Tennis for Two”. In 1962 students in the USA developed the space game **Spacewar!** on a mainframe computer. Computers like that were huge and found only at universities. The engineer **Ralph Baer** developed the first home video game console, which came out in 1972 as the **Magnavox Odyssey**. It was connected to the television.

In 1972 the company Atari brought out **Pong**, a simple game that imitates table tennis. It was a great success in pubs and amusement arcades. There stood **arcade machines**, which you played by putting in coins. “Space Invaders” followed in 1978 and “**Pac-Man**” in 1980, in which a yellow figure eats dots and is chased by ghosts. The 1980s are regarded as the golden age of the arcades.

In 1981 the Japanese game developer **Shigeru Miyamoto** invented a little figure in the game “Donkey Kong” who was later called Mario. **Mario** was originally a plumber and became the most famous video game hero. In 1985 “Super Mario Bros.” came out for the Nintendo console NES and was a worldwide success. In 1986 came “The Legend of Zelda” with the hero **Link**, also by Miyamoto. This made Nintendo one of the most important games companies.

**Tetris** was invented in 1984 by the programmer Alexey Pajitnov in Moscow, in what was then the **Soviet Union**. You arrange falling blocks so that full rows disappear. In 1989 Nintendo brought out the portable **Game Boy**, and Tetris came with many of them. In 1996 the first **Pokémon** games for the Game Boy came out in Japan; in them Pikachu is an Electric-type Pokémon. Pokémon became one of the most successful game series of all.

In the 1990s consoles such as the Sony **PlayStation** arrived, and games became three-dimensional. From the 2000s people played **online** more and more often with others all over the world. In 2006 the Nintendo Wii, with its motion controls, made gaming a family activity. With smartphones, from about 2008 games became available to almost everyone, always and everywhere. In 2017 the Nintendo Switch came out, which can be used at home and on the move.

**Minecraft** was developed by the Swede Markus Persson and officially released in 2011. In its world of blocks you can build almost anything, and Minecraft is one of the best-selling games of all time. In 2014 Microsoft bought Mojang, the company that makes the game. Today millions of people meet in online games, and **e-sports** tournaments fill stadiums. Museums and exhibitions, including in Switzerland, show the history of video games.

begriffe.erklaerung: A device for playing games that you connect to the television or hold in your hand.
A large coin-operated game machine that people used to play in amusement arcades.
An early computer as big as a room.
A single dot of the picture on the screen.
A portable games console such as the Game Boy.

gewusst: In “Donkey Kong” Mario was at first called “Jumpman” because jumping was mainly what he could do.
The name Pac-Man comes from the Japanese expression “paku paku”, which imitates a snapping sound when eating.
The first Game Boy had a screen that could only show shades of green.

teile.einleitung: On sports day the whole school spends a day outdoors with games, races and competitions. It is all about exercise, team spirit and lots of fun.
wichtigste: In tug of war two teams pull on a long rope.
In the sack race you hop to the finish in a sack.
In the relay each child runs part of the distance.
In the egg-and-spoon race you carry an egg on a spoon.
In the three-legged race two children tie one leg each together.
On sunny days a cap and sun cream protect you.
At the end there is often a certificate or a medal.

abschnitte.text: On sports day there is often a **sprint** over a short distance. The **relay** is very popular. In it several children run one after the other. Each runs part of the distance and then hands over to the next, often with a baton. The winning team is the one whose last runner reaches the finish first.

In **tug of war** two teams stand at the ends of a long rope. In the middle there is a line on the ground. At a signal both teams pull. Whoever pulls the other team over the line wins. It helps if everyone pulls at the same moment.

In the **sack race** you climb into a sack and hop to the finish. In the **egg-and-spoon race** you balance an egg on a spoon. If it falls off, you put it back on. In the **three-legged race** two legs of two children are tied together. Then together they have three legs and have to run in step.

On a sunny sports day a **cap** or a hat protects your head. **Sun cream** is part of it too. A water bottle is also important, because you sweat when you move. Comfortable trainers and clothes you can move well in make the day more pleasant.

At the end of sports day there is often a **prize-giving**. Many children receive a **certificate** or a medal. But even more important than winning is that everyone takes part, cheers each other on and stays fair.

gewusst: Tug of war used to be an Olympic sport.
The word “Stafette” (relay) comes from Italian and used to mean a messenger on horseback.

teile.einleitung: Fair play means keeping to the rules in sport and respecting team-mates, opponents and referees. The expression comes from English and simply means playing fairly. Fair play is more important than any win, because without fairness sport is no fun for anyone.
wichtigste: Fair play means keeping to the rules and respecting others.
After the game you shake hands with your opponent.
If an opponent is lying injured on the ground, you kick the ball out of play.
Whoever has lost congratulates the winner fairly.
A dive, that is a faked foul, is unfair.
Doping, that is taking banned substances, goes against fair play.
Fair spectators respect both teams.

abschnitte.text: **Fair play** is more than just following the rules of the game. It means seeing your opponent as a partner without whom there would be no game. It includes honesty, respect and helpfulness. Anyone who plays fairly wants to win only through their own performance and not through tricks or cheating.

Before and after the game the teams shake hands. If an opponent is lying injured on the ground, you kick the ball out of play so that they can be treated. Afterwards the other team gives the ball back. A **dive** is a faked foul meant to fool the referee, and it is considered unfair. Insulting people or deliberately injuring them also has nothing to do with fair play.

Winning and losing are part of sport. Whoever loses congratulates the **winner** and is a good loser. Whoever wins is happy without laughing at the opponent. Respect also applies to the **referee**, even if you do not agree with their decision.

**Doping** means taking banned substances to become stronger or faster. It is one of the most serious breaches of fair play because it puts honest athletes at a disadvantage and harms your health. Fixed match results are also cheating. In Switzerland the programme “cool and clean” by Swiss Olympic campaigns for fair and clean sport.

abschnitte.titel: Fair play among fans and awards
abschnitte.text: Spectators can be fair too, if they respect both teams and applaud good moves by both sides. Booing the national anthem or insults are not part of it. Many associations give **fair play awards**, for example FIFA or the International Olympic Committee. At the 2018 football World Cup a fair play ranking based on fewer yellow cards even decided that Japan went through instead of Senegal.

begriffe.erklaerung: Fair behaviour in sport, with respect for rules and people.
A faked foul in which you deliberately let yourself fall.
Regard and consideration for other people.
Taking banned substances to improve performance.
The person who makes sure that everyone keeps to the rules.

gewusst: In Ultimate Frisbee there are usually no referees; the players decide fouls themselves, fairly.
The International Olympic Committee awards a Pierre de Coubertin medal for especially fair behaviour.
At the Olympic Games athletes take an oath in which they promise to compete fairly.

teile.einleitung: Sport is more than exercise. It brings people together, promotes health and plays an important role in schools, clubs and politics. In Switzerland the Confederation, the cantons and the federations support sport in many ways.
wichtigste: Since 1972 the programme “Youth and Sport” (J+S) has promoted sport for children and young people.
Swiss Olympic is the umbrella organisation of the Swiss sports federations and the National Olympic Committee.
Adults are recommended to do at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise per week.
Children and teenagers should be active for about one hour a day.
In summer 2025 the Women's European Football Championship took place in Switzerland.
To combat violence at sporting events there is the cantons' hooligan agreement.

abschnitte.text: **Youth and Sport (J+S)** is the Confederation's largest sports promotion programme. It began in **1972** and replaced the military-style pre-training. Unlike before, it was open to girls too. J+S supports courses and camps in clubs and schools and trains leaders. Every year hundreds of thousands of children and young people take part. It is the responsibility of the **Federal Office of Sport** in Magglingen.

**Swiss Olympic** unites the Swiss sports federations and represents Switzerland at the International Olympic Committee. Every sport has its own federation, for example Swiss Athletics for athletics. Many top athletes pursue a **dual career**: they train and at the same time do an apprenticeship, study or work. Sports schools help to combine the two.

Regular exercise strengthens the heart, muscles and bones and is also good for the mind. The **Swiss exercise recommendations** advise adults to do at least **150 minutes** of moderate or 75 minutes of vigorous exercise per week. For children and teenagers the guideline is about **one hour a day**. This includes cycling, playing and walking.

Sport brings together people from different backgrounds. In **clubs** many volunteers help out as coaches, helpers or on the committee. **Special Olympics** offers training and competitions for people with intellectual disabilities, and the **Paralympics** mainly for people with physical disabilities. The biggest festival of grassroots sport is the **Federal Gymnastics Festival**, held in Lausanne in 2025.

Switzerland has hosted big tournaments several times. In 1954 the men's football World Cup took place here, and in July **2025** the **Women's European Championship** was held in eight cities. Unfortunately, there is sometimes violence at some matches. That is why the cantons agreed on the **hooligan agreement** (Hooligan-Konkordat). It allows, for example, **area bans**, that is bans on being near a stadium.

gewusst: The Federal Gymnastics Festival takes place about every six years and attracts tens of thousands of gymnasts.
Many international sports federations and the International Olympic Committee have their headquarters in Switzerland, especially in Lausanne.

teile.einleitung: The Berlin Wall was a heavily guarded border barrier that separated West Berlin from the GDR and East Berlin from 1961 to 1989. It became the symbol of the division of Germany and Europe in the Cold War. On the evening of 9 November 1989 it opened unexpectedly after a misleading announcement.
wichtigste: The GDR began building the wall on 13 August 1961.
It surrounded West Berlin over a length of about 155 kilometres.
With the wall, the GDR wanted to stop its citizens from fleeing to the West.
At least 140 people died at the wall.
On 9 November 1989 the wall was opened.
The trigger was a misleading announcement of new travel rules by Günter Schabowski.
On 3 October 1990 Germany was reunified.

abschnitte.text: After the Second World War Germany was divided into two states, the **Federal Republic** in the west and the **GDR** in the east. Berlin lay in the middle of the GDR and was also divided. By 1961 millions of people had fled from the GDR to the West via West Berlin. To stop this, the GDR leaders had the border sealed off on the night of 12 to 13 August 1961.

Over time a barbed wire fence became a multiple barrier made of concrete. Between the inner and outer walls lay the so-called **death strip**, with watchtowers, dog runs and bright lamps. The border guards had orders to shoot at people trying to escape. Even so, many people managed to flee, for example through tunnels or hidden in cars.

In the autumn of 1989 hundreds of thousands of people in the GDR demonstrated peacefully for freedom. On the evening of 9 November, Politburo member **Günter Schabowski** announced new travel rules at a press conference. When asked from when they would apply, he said by mistake: “immediately, without delay”. Thousands of East Berliners poured to the border crossings, and the barriers were opened first at **Bornholmer Strasse**.

People from East and West celebrated together on the wall. In the following months the wall was torn down, and many people chipped off pieces as souvenirs. On **3 October 1990** the two German states were reunified. The fall of the wall also stands for the end of the **Cold War** between East and West.

abschnitte.titel: What can still be seen today
abschnitte.text: In some places in Berlin, remains of the wall still stand. The **East Side Gallery** is a stretch over a kilometre long that artists from all over the world have painted. At the former border crossing **Checkpoint Charlie**, a museum recalls the time of division. In Bernauer Strasse a memorial shows what the death strip looked like.

begriffe.erklaerung: German Democratic Republic, the East German state from 1949 to 1990.
Tension between West and East after 1945, without a direct war between the great powers.
The guarded strip between the walls in which people trying to escape were shot at.
The joining together of East and West Germany in 1990.

gewusst: The wall stood for 28 years, and on 5 February 2018 it had been gone for exactly as long as it had stood.
After 1990 many parts of the wall were given away or sold to other countries and now stand all over the world.

teile.einleitung: Unihockey is a fast team game played with a stick and a light ball with holes. It is very popular in Switzerland, especially among children and teenagers. Internationally the sport is called floorball.
wichtigste: On a large court each team has five outfield players and a goalkeeper.
The goalkeeper plays without a stick.
A match lasts three periods of 20 minutes each.
The official ball has 26 holes.
In English Unihockey is called floorball.
Heading the ball is not allowed.
The Swiss women became world champions for the first time in 2005.

abschnitte.text: Two teams try to shoot the ball into the opponents' goal with their **sticks**. On the **large court** each team has **five outfield players and a goalkeeper**. A match lasts **three periods of 20 minutes each**, with breaks in between. There is also **small-court** floorball with fewer players, which is often played in school gyms.

The floorball goalkeeper has **no stick**. They stop the ball with their body and may catch it with their hands inside the **goal area**. They wear a mask that protects the face and padded clothing. Because the ball can travel very fast, they need good reflexes.

The ball is made of plastic, hollow and has **26 holes**. It is very light and can therefore fly very fast. Outfield players may **not** play the ball **with their head** and may not lift their stick too high. These rules protect against dangerous situations with sticks at head height.

Internationally the sport is called **floorball**, and the world federation is the **International Floorball Federation**. Switzerland is one of the strongest nations. The Swiss women won their first world title **in Singapore in 2005** and became world champions for the second time **in the Czech Republic in 2025**. Many municipalities have floorball clubs for children.

gewusst: In its present form floorball comes from Sweden.
An official floorball ball weighs only about 23 grams.

teile.einleitung: Speed is the ability to react very quickly and to move fast. It is especially important in sprinting, but also in ball games. Speed depends on muscles, nerves and technique.
wichtigste: Reaction time is the time between the starting signal and the first movement.
Anyone who reacts faster than 0.1 seconds has made a false start.
Sprinters start from a crouch start using starting blocks.
Fast-twitch muscle fibres are important for quick movements.
Running speed comes from stride length and stride frequency.
Mujinga Kambundji became world indoor champion over 60 metres in 2022.

abschnitte.text: **Reaction time** begins with the starting signal and ends when the sprinter moves in the starting blocks. Good sprinters react in about one to two **tenths of a second**. According to the rules of **World Athletics**, a human cannot react to the gun faster than **0.1 seconds**. A faster reaction therefore counts as a **false start**. Sensors in the starting blocks measure this precisely.

In the 100 metres, sprinters start from a **crouch start**. They support themselves with their hands on the ground and press their feet into the **starting blocks**. At the signal they push off powerfully. In this way they can accelerate quickly. At school the standing start is often practised first.

**Fast-twitch muscle fibres** are important for fast, explosive movements. They contract quickly and powerfully but tire quickly. Good sprinters have a lot of them. Running speed comes from **stride length** times **stride frequency**. Anyone who takes longer or more frequent strides runs faster.

**Mujinga Kambundji** is one of the most successful Swiss sprinters. In **2022** she won gold over **60 metres** at the World Indoor Championships in **Belgrade**. Indoors there is no 100-metre track, which is why the 60 metres is the shortest sprint there. Her success has got many young people in Switzerland excited about athletics.

gewusst: Speed can be trained particularly well in children, for example with tag games and relays.
In a sprint breathing is often hardly needed, because the energy for a few seconds comes from the stores in the muscle.

teile.einleitung: Tango is a dance and a kind of music from South America. It began on the Río de la Plata in Buenos Aires and Montevideo. Today it is danced all over the world, including in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Tango began at the end of the 19th century in Buenos Aires (Argentina) and Montevideo (Uruguay).
Immigrants from Europe and influences from Africa shaped the new music.
The bandoneon is the typical instrument of tango.
Astor Piazzolla renewed tango with jazz and classical music: “Tango Nuevo”.
Since 2009 tango has been part of UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage.

abschnitte.text: Tango began in the **harbour districts** of Buenos Aires and Montevideo. These two cities lie on the **Río de la Plata**, a large river estuary. At that time many **immigrants** came to South America from Italy, Spain and other countries. They brought their music with them, and it mixed with rhythms from Africa and South America. Out of this mixture, step by step, tango was born.

The **bandoneon** is a squeezebox instrument, similar to an accordion. It was invented in **Germany** in the 19th century and is named after the music teacher Heinrich Band. Emigrants took it to South America. Its slightly melancholy sound became the heart of tango. It is often joined by the violin, piano and double bass.

Tango is danced in pairs in a close hold. The dancers **improvise** a lot: one person leads, the other follows. Typical are slow, creeping steps and sudden pauses. There is also tango as a competition dance in dance schools. In many cities tango fans meet at dance evenings called **milongas**.

The Argentine composer **Astor Piazzolla** played the bandoneon himself. He combined tango with **jazz** and **classical music**. This new style is called **Tango Nuevo**, meaning “new tango”. At first some fans of the old tango found it too modern. Today his pieces are played in concert halls all over the world.

gewusst: Argentina and Uruguay applied to UNESCO for the listing together.
The bandoneon has no keys like a piano but many buttons on both sides.

teile.einleitung: A fairy tale is an imaginative story in which miracles happen, animals talk and witches, dwarfs or fairies appear. Fairy tales usually begin with “Once upon a time” and end happily, because good wins over evil. The best-known German fairy tales were written down by the Brothers Grimm.
wichtigste: Fairy tales are imaginative stories with magic and miracles.
Many well-known German fairy tales were written down by the Brothers Grimm.
In fairy tales good usually wins over evil in the end.
Little Red Riding Hood meets a wolf in the forest.
Snow White's seven dwarfs live together.
Sleeping Beauty sleeps for a hundred years.
Rumpelstiltskin spins gold out of straw.
The Town Musicians of Bremen include a donkey.

abschnitte.text: A **fairy tale** is an invented story in which the marvellous is taken for granted. Animals talk, people are put under spells, and there are giants, dwarfs, fairies and witches. Fairy tales often begin with “Once upon a time” and end with words like “and they lived happily ever after”. Place and time usually remain vague, somewhere in a forest or a kingdom. The characters are clearly good or evil.

**Magic numbers** often appear in fairy tales, above all three, seven and twelve. So there are seven dwarfs, three wishes or twelve brothers. The heroines and heroes have to pass difficult **tests** and are helped along the way, for example by animals or magic objects. In the end good is rewarded and evil punished. These clear patterns make fairy tales easy to understand and easy to remember.

The brothers **Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm** were German language scholars. They collected stories that people told each other and in 1812 published the first volume of their “**Children's and Household Tales**”. It contains over 200 fairy tales, including “Little Red Riding Hood”, “Hansel and Gretel” and “Snow White”. Wilhelm Grimm revised the texts several times and made them more suitable for children.
