Today the collection is part of UNESCO's **Memory of the World** register.

**Little Red Riding Hood** meets a wolf in the forest who later eats her grandmother. Hansel and Gretel find a gingerbread house in which a **witch** lives. Snow White finds refuge with seven dwarfs, and Sleeping Beauty sleeps for a hundred years after a curse. The prince climbs up Rapunzel's long hair into the tower. The little man **Rumpelstiltskin** spins gold out of straw, and the Town Musicians of Bremen, a donkey, a dog, a cat and a cockerel, drive away robbers.

abschnitte.titel: Fairy tales from around the world
abschnitte.text: There are fairy tales in every culture. In France Charles **Perrault** wrote down fairy tales such as “Cinderella” and “Puss in Boots” as early as 1697. The Dane **Hans Christian Andersen** invented his own fairy tales such as “The Little Mermaid” and “The Ugly Duckling”; fairy tales invented by an author like this are called **literary fairy tales**. The stories from “One Thousand and One Nights”, with Aladdin and Sinbad, come from the Middle East. In Switzerland, too, folk tales were collected in the 19th century.

Many fairy tales have been filmed by Disney and other studios, for example “Snow White” in 1937 or “Frozen”, based on Andersen's “The Snow Queen”. Fairy tales are told as plays, audio dramas and picture books. Experts think fairy tales help children cope with fears, because good wins in the end. Some fairy tales, however, are rather cruel because they come from another time. Today they are often retold in new and modern ways.

begriffe.erklaerung: A fairy tale that was passed on by word of mouth for a long time, with no known author.
A fairy tale invented by a particular author.
A number such as three or seven that often appears in fairy tales.
An evil spell that harms someone.

gewusst: In the fairy tale, the Town Musicians of Bremen never actually arrive in Bremen.
In the Brothers Grimm's first version of Snow White, the wicked one was still her own mother; later she became the stepmother.
In Bremen there is a bronze statue of the Town Musicians, and it is said that touching the donkey's legs brings good luck.

teile.einleitung: In orienteering you run through forests and open country with a map and a compass. You have to find a series of control points as quickly as possible. So you need fast legs and a clever head.
wichtigste: A control flag is divided diagonally into orange and white.
Orienteering maps usually have a scale of 1:15 000 or 1:10 000.
Yellow means open land, blue water, green dense forest.
Brown contour lines close together show steep ground.
When orienting the map, you turn it so that it matches the terrain.
Simone Niggli won 23 World Championship gold medals.

abschnitte.text: In **orienteering** you are given a map on which the **controls** are marked. You have to visit them in the right order. You choose the route yourself. Each control is marked with a **control flag**, which is divided diagonally into **orange and white**. That way it is easy to see in the forest, and you punch in there electronically.

Orienteering maps are very precise and usually have a **scale of 1:15 000** or 1:10 000. At 1:15 000, one centimetre on the map equals 150 metres on the ground. The colours have fixed meanings: **yellow** is open land such as meadows, **blue** is water, **green** dense forest. White means forest that is easy to run through. Rocks and stones are marked in black.

abschnitte.titel: Contour lines and orienting the map
abschnitte.text: Brown **contour lines** join points of the same height. If they are **close together**, the ground is steep. If they are far apart, it is flat. When **orienting** the map, you turn it so that its north matches north on the ground. Then the directions on the map correspond to those in nature.

Switzerland is very successful at orienteering. **Simone Niggli-Luder** from the canton of Bern won a total of **23 world titles**. She is regarded as one of the best orienteers of all time. In many schools orienteering is part of PE lessons. There are also school sports championships and family orienteering events for all ages.

gewusst: Besides running in the forest there is also sprint orienteering in towns, mountain bike orienteering and ski orienteering.
The Swiss national maps from swisstopo are regarded worldwide as particularly accurate.

teile.einleitung: The tempo tells you how fast a piece of music is played. Composers usually write Italian words above the music for this. These tempo markings are understood all over the world.
wichtigste: Largo, Lento and Grave stand for very slow tempos.
Moderato means moderate, so neither slow nor fast.
Vivace means lively, Presto very fast.
Prestissimo is the fastest common tempo.
“A tempo” means: back to the original tempo.
Rubato means shaping the tempo freely, letting it vary slightly.

abschnitte.text: **Grave** means “heavy, serious” and is very slow and weighty. **Largo** means “broad” and is also very slow. **Lento** simply means “slow”. A little faster is **Adagio**, and after that comes **Andante**, a walking tempo. Slow movements often sound solemn, calm or sad.

**Moderato** comes from the Italian word for “moderate”. The tempo is neither slow nor fast. **Allegretto** is a little faster and sounds cheerful. Medium tempos like these suit songs and dances well. Often there is a second word as well, for example “Allegro moderato”, meaning moderately fast.

**Allegro** means fast and lively. **Vivace** means “lively” and is quick and spirited. **Presto** is very fast. The ending **-issimo** makes a word stronger: **Prestissimo** means “as fast as possible”, and **Larghissimo** is even slower than Largo. Fast movements require a lot of practice and good technique.

Sometimes the tempo is meant to change during a piece. With **ritardando** you slow down, with **accelerando** you speed up. If **a tempo** follows, you return to the previous basic tempo. **Rubato** means “robbed”: you take a little time here and give it back there. This is typical of Romantic piano music, for example by Frédéric Chopin.

gewusst: Italian tempo words have been used since the 17th century because Italy was very influential in music at that time.
A movement of a larger piece is often named after its tempo, for example “the Adagio”.

teile.einleitung: A video game is a game that runs on a screen and is controlled with a controller, keyboard or touchscreen. It is played on consoles, computers or mobile phones. Children all over the world today know characters such as Mario, Pikachu or Sonic.
wichtigste: Mario has a brother called Luigi.
In Tetris you arrange falling blocks into full rows.
Pac-Man is chased by ghosts.
The Pokémon Pikachu is yellow.
The world of Minecraft is made of cubes.
Sonic is a blue hedgehog, Donkey Kong a gorilla.
The PEGI number on the box shows the suitable age.

abschnitte.text: One of the first successful video games was **Pong** from 1972, a simple form of table tennis. In 1980 **Pac-Man** came out, a yellow circle that eats dots and is chased by four ghosts. In 1981 “Donkey Kong” appeared, in which a gorilla throws barrels. It was the first appearance of the character who was later called Mario. In 1984 Alexey Pajitnov invented the game **Tetris**, in which you arrange falling blocks.

**Mario** is an Italian plumber with a red cap and a moustache, and his brother is Luigi. In “Mario Kart” the two of them race cars with friends. The blue hedgehog **Sonic** from the company Sega has been known since 1991 and is especially fast. **Pikachu** is a yellow Pokémon that can produce electricity. The Pokémon games first came out in Japan in 1996 for the Game Boy.

In **Minecraft** the whole world is made of cubes that you can mine and put together again. The game was developed by the Swede Markus Persson and is one of the best-selling games in the world. You can build houses, castles or whole cities. Many schools use an education edition, for example to practise maths or history. Games with a lot of freedom like this are called **open-world** or sandbox games.

The **PEGI number** on the box shows from what age a game is suitable. The levels are 3, 7, 12, 16 and 18 years. Small symbols also show whether a game contains violence or gambling, for example. In Switzerland a federal law on protecting minors with regard to films and video games obliges retailers to respect these age limits. Experts advise taking breaks and agreeing fixed playing times.

Video games are a huge business today and earn more money than the film industry. In **e-sports** professionals compete against each other in tournaments, sometimes in front of thousands of spectators. Many games are played online with friends all over the world. There are also educational games, puzzle games and games that tell stories like a film. Some games are partly free and make money from purchases in the game.

begriffe.erklaerung: A European system for age ratings of games.
Video games as competitions with tournaments.
A section or stage in a game.
A game world in which you can move around freely.

gewusst: In his first appearance, in the game “Donkey Kong”, Mario was still called Jumpman.
The name Pac-Man comes from the Japanese expression “paku paku”, which imitates a munching sound.
In 2014 Microsoft bought the company behind Minecraft for 2.5 billion US dollars.

teile.einleitung: You can get injured during sport, for example through a fall, a collision or too much strain. A distinction is made between acute injuries and overuse injuries, which develop slowly.
wichtigste: A distortion is a sprain of a joint.
A luxation is a dislocated joint.
In medicine a bruise is called a contusion.
The menisci absorb shocks in the knee.
A sudden stabbing muscle pain during a sprint points to a torn muscle fibre.
Too many jumps can cause jumper's knee.
An inflamed bursa is called bursitis.

abschnitte.text: In a **distortion**, that is a sprain, a joint is moved beyond its normal range. In the process, ligaments and the joint capsule are overstretched. Twisting your ankle is typical. In a **luxation** the joint surfaces lose contact with each other completely, often at the shoulder. A dislocated joint may only be put back in place by **professionals**.

In a **contusion** or bruise, tissue is crushed by a blunt blow without the skin being injured. This causes pain, swelling and a **haematoma** (a bruise under the skin). In a **torn muscle fibre**, individual muscle fibres tear, often during sudden sprints. The pain comes suddenly and is stabbing. Then you must stop immediately.

In the knee joint there are two **menisci**. They are crescent-shaped discs of cartilage that act as **shock absorbers** between the thigh bone and the shin bone. They can tear during twisting movements under load. **Jumper's knee** is an overload of the tendon directly below the kneecap. It often occurs in volleyball and basketball players who jump a lot.

Some problems develop slowly through too much strain. With **shin splints** the inner edge of the shin bone hurts, usually because the amount of running was increased too quickly. In **bursitis** a **bursa** becomes inflamed: a small cushion that reduces friction between bones and tendons. Rest and a slower increase in training help.

For many acute injuries the **PECH rule** helps: Pause (rest), Eis (ice), compression (a light pressure bandage) and Hochlagern (elevation); in English it is often called RICE. If the pain is severe, the joint looks out of place or you can no longer move it, you should see a doctor. You can prevent injuries by **warming up**, using good technique, suitable equipment and getting enough rest.

gewusst: With the PECH rule, you never put the ice directly on the skin but wrap it in a cloth.
Many medical terms for injuries come from Latin, for example luxation from “luxare”, to dislocate.

teile.einleitung: Swimming in a lake, a river or a swimming pool is fun, but it can be dangerous. That is why the Swiss Lifesaving Society SLRG has drawn up six swimming safety rules. If you know them and follow them, you stay safe in the water.
wichtigste: The SLRG has six swimming safety rules.
Small children only go to the water with an adult and stay within arm's reach.
You never swim with a very full or a completely empty stomach.
If you are overheated, you cool down first before going into the water.
Lilos and armbands do not belong in deep water.
You never swim long distances alone.

abschnitte.text: The **SLRG** is the Swiss Lifesaving Society. It works to make sure that fewer people drown. It trains lifeguards and informs people about dangers in the water. Its **six swimming safety rules** are known all over Switzerland. You can find them at many bathing spots and in swimming pools.

The first rule concerns children: they only go to the water **accompanied**, and small children stay within **arm's reach**. So the person supervising should be able to grab the child immediately. This is because small children often drown **very quietly**. They can no longer shout or wave, which is why people sometimes do not notice. Anyone keeping watch therefore always looks and does not let themselves be distracted.

You never go into the water after drinking alcohol and never with a very **full** or a completely **empty stomach**. Both can weaken the body. If you are very **overheated**, you do not jump straight into cold water. The body needs time to get used to the cold. You also do not jump into murky or unknown waters, because there may be stones or branches under the surface.

**Lilos** (air mattresses) and **armbands** do not belong in deep water. They can drift away or lose air and offer no safety there. You **never** swim long distances **alone**. Even good swimmers can suddenly get tired or get cramp. Then it is important that someone is nearby who can help.

gewusst: The SLRG was founded in 1933.
In rivers such as the Rhine or the Aare the current is often much stronger than it looks from above.

teile.einleitung: Flexibility is the ability to carry out movements with a large range. Like strength and endurance, it is one of the important abilities in sport. It also helps in everyday life, for example when bending down or getting dressed.
wichtigste: Flexibility is made up of joint mobility and stretchability.
Rhythmic gymnastics requires very great flexibility.
Children are naturally very flexible.
Without training, flexibility decreases with age.
The “sit and reach” test checks the back and the backs of the thighs.
Muscles that are permanently shortened limit flexibility.

abschnitte.text: Flexibility is made up of two parts. **Joint mobility** concerns the range of movement of the joints. It depends on how the bones and joints are built. **Stretchability** concerns the muscles, tendons and ligaments. Together they determine how far you can bend, stretch or twist.

**Children** are naturally very flexible. If they do not train it, their flexibility decreases with age. That is why it is worth doing gymnastics, climbing and stretching regularly from childhood. What you look after when you are young is easier to keep. But adults can become more flexible too; it just takes longer.

In some sports flexibility is especially important. In **rhythmic gymnastics** the gymnasts show splits and extreme stretching positions. In the **splits** the legs lie stretched out on the floor to the front and back or to the sides. Dance, artistic gymnastics, martial arts and swimming also demand a lot of flexibility. In other sports it helps you to carry out movements cleanly and powerfully.

The **sit and reach** test is used to check flexibility. You sit with your legs straight and reach forward as far as possible. The further you get past your feet, the more flexible your hips, back and **hamstrings** at the back of your thighs are. If a muscle is permanently **shortened**, the joint can no longer move fully. Regular movement and stretching counteract this.

gewusst: Sitting for long periods, for example at school or in front of a screen, can shorten certain muscles over time.
On average girls and women are a little more flexible than boys and men.

teile.einleitung: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was one of the most famous composers of all time. He was born in Salzburg in 1756, was a child prodigy and wrote over 600 works in his short life. Operas such as “The Magic Flute” and pieces such as “Eine kleine Nachtmusik” are still known all over the world today.
wichtigste: Mozart was born in Salzburg on 27 January 1756.
His father Leopold taught him when he was still a small child.
At about the age of five he composed his first little pieces.
Together with Haydn and Beethoven he is one of the Viennese Classical composers.
His opera “The Magic Flute” features the bird catcher Papageno.
Mozart died in Vienna in 1791 at the age of only 35.
His Requiem was unfinished when he died.

abschnitte.text: Mozart was born on 27 January 1756 in **Salzburg**, which at that time did not yet belong to Austria. His father **Leopold Mozart** was a musician and taught him and his older sister Maria Anna, known as Nannerl. Wolfgang was already playing the keyboard at the age of three, and at about five he wrote his first little pieces. He also played the violin and could sight-read difficult music.

The father travelled with his two **child prodigies** through many countries in Europe. The family played at royal courts in Munich, Vienna, Paris and London. On the journey home in 1766 they also stopped in Switzerland, among other places in Geneva, Lausanne, Bern and Zurich. Later Mozart travelled to Italy several times, where he wrote operas and learned a great deal. The long carriage journeys were tiring, and the children were often ill.

In 1781 Mozart moved to **Vienna** and worked there as a freelance musician, which was unusual at the time. He married Constanze Weber, gave concerts and lessons and wrote many works. Sometimes he earned well, sometimes he had money worries. He died in Vienna on 5 December 1791, only 35 years old, probably of an illness.

Mozart's best-known operas include “The Marriage of Figaro”, “Don Giovanni” and **“The Magic Flute”** with the funny bird catcher Papageno. He wrote over 40 symphonies, many piano concertos and chamber music. “**Eine kleine Nachtmusik**” is one of the best-known pieces of classical music of all. His last work, the **Requiem**, a mass for the dead, remained unfinished and was completed by a pupil.

So that Mozart's works can be found easily, Ludwig von Köchel arranged them in 1862 in the order in which they were written. This **Köchel catalogue** gives each work a number with the abbreviation K. (in German KV). “Eine kleine Nachtmusik”, for example, has the number K. 525, the Requiem K. 626. Today you can visit Mozart's birthplace in Salzburg, and the city holds a Mozart Week every year.

begriffe.erklaerung: Someone who invents music and writes it down.
A child who shows extraordinary abilities very early.
A stage play in which the performers sing instead of speaking.
A mass in memory of the dead, also called a mass for the dead.
The list of all of Mozart's works with numbers, abbreviated K. or KV.

gewusst: Mozart's full baptismal name was Joannes Chrysostomus Wolfgangus Theophilus Mozart.
As a child Mozart also visited Zurich and Bern with his family in 1766.
The famous chocolate Mozartkugeln were only invented about 100 years after his death.

teile.einleitung: Rock music is a genre that began in the 1950s in the USA with rock 'n' roll. Typical features are the electric guitar, powerful drums, the bass guitar and energetic singing. Rock became the music of young people and has split into many styles such as hard rock, punk and metal.
wichtigste: Rock 'n' roll developed in the 1950s in the USA.
Elvis Presley was called the “King of Rock 'n' Roll”.
The electric guitar especially shapes the sound of rock music.
The Beatles came from Liverpool.
The British band Queen released “Bohemian Rhapsody” in 1975.
Punk in the 1970s was known for short, fast and rough songs.
The Ticino hard rock band Gotthard is named after an Alpine pass.

abschnitte.text: Rock music developed in the 1950s in the USA from blues, rhythm and blues and country. This early style is called **rock 'n' roll**. Musicians such as Chuck Berry, Little Richard and above all **Elvis Presley**, the “King of Rock 'n' Roll”, thrilled young people. At the time many adults found the music and Elvis's wild hip-swinging scandalous.

In the 1960s British bands conquered the world. The **Beatles** from Liverpool became the most successful band of all time, and the Rolling Stones sounded rougher and more rebellious. After that came bands such as Led Zeppelin, Pink Floyd and **Queen**, who released the song “Bohemian Rhapsody” in 1975. Guitarists such as Jimi Hendrix showed everything you can do with an electric guitar.

The most important instrument is the **electric guitar**, whose sound is made loud through an amplifier and often distorted with effects. Then there are the bass guitar, the drums and sometimes keyboards. A typical rock band has four or five members. Rock songs usually have a powerful beat and striking guitar figures, which are called **riffs**.

Many styles grew out of rock. **Hard rock** and heavy metal sound especially loud and hard, for example with AC/DC or Black Sabbath. **Punk** in the 1970s, with bands such as the Ramones and the Sex Pistols, was known for short, fast and rough songs. In the 1990s grunge became famous with Nirvana from Seattle, and later came indie rock and alternative rock.

Switzerland has successful rock bands too. The hard rock band **Gotthard** was founded in Lugano in 1992 and is named after the Gotthard Pass; it has topped the Swiss hit parade several times. **Krokus** from Solothurn is one of the best-known Swiss hard rock bands and was also successful in the USA. In Switzerland rock concerts take place, for example, at the Openair St Gallen or the Greenfield Festival in Interlaken.

begriffe.erklaerung: An early rock style of the 1950s from the USA.
A short, often repeated guitar figure that shapes a song.
A device that makes the sound of an electric guitar loud.
A rock style of the 1970s with short, fast and rough songs.

gewusst: “Bohemian Rhapsody” lasts almost six minutes and has no real chorus, but it still became a worldwide hit.
In 1969 the Beatles played their last public concert on the roof of their office building in London.
The first electric guitar with a solid wooden body went into series production in the early 1950s.

teile.einleitung: **Rhythm** is what makes music good for dancing, clapping and marching. It comes from long and short notes that combine into a pattern. You can also make rhythm without any instruments at all, just with your own body.
wichtigste: A rhythm is a sequence of long and short notes.
The first beat in a bar is usually stressed most strongly.
Music made by clapping, stamping and clicking your fingers is called body percussion.
The word “pineapple” has three syllables, so you clap three times.
The cajón is a wooden box that you sit on and drum on with your hands.
You strike claves against each other; a rattle has to be shaken.

abschnitte.text: A **rhythm** is a sequence of **long and short notes**. Underneath it there is often a steady **basic beat**, like the ticking of a clock or our heartbeat. Several beats together form a **bar**. The **first beat** in the bar is usually stressed most strongly. You can easily walk in step to a **march** because the basic beat is so clear.

In **body percussion** you make music with your own body: **clapping**, **stamping**, **clicking your fingers** or slapping your thighs. In **echo clapping** someone claps a rhythm and everyone claps it back. This trains your hearing and memory. You can do it anywhere, without any instruments.

Every word has its own rhythm. If you clap **“pineapple”** in syllables, you clap three times: pine-ap-ple. “Apple” has two syllables, and so does “kiwi”. Long words such as “chocolate cake” give exciting rhythms. In this way even small children learn to hear and copy rhythms.

The **cajón** is a wooden box that you sit on and drum on with your hands. It comes from Peru. **Claves** are two wooden sticks that you **strike against each other**. A **rattle** has to be **shaken** so that the grains inside make a sound. The drum, tambourine and triangle are also popular rhythm instruments.

In Basel **drumming** has a long tradition. At the Basel carnival drummers and piccolo players march through the streets and play difficult rhythms from memory. At the **Trychle** custom in Central Switzerland, too, many people shake their large bells in the same rhythm. Rhythm brings people together when everyone keeps time together.

gewusst: Our heart beats in its own rhythm, usually about 60 to 100 times a minute at rest.
Some rhythms are so well known that you can recognise a song just from the clapping.

teile.einleitung: A cartoon is a film made of many drawn pictures. If the pictures are shown quickly one after the other, it looks as if the characters are moving. Today many animated films are made on the computer, such as “Toy Story” or “Frozen”.
wichtigste: Movement appears when many pictures are shown quickly one after the other.
Walt Disney's first feature-length cartoon was “Snow White” from 1937.
In 1995 “Toy Story” was the first cinema film made entirely on the computer.
In “The Lion King” the lion cub is called Simba, and Pumbaa is a warthog.
The snowman in “Frozen” is called Olaf.
Nemo is a clownfish, Woody a cowboy and Baloo a bear.
Maya the Bee's best friend is called Willy.

abschnitte.text: A cartoon consists of many single pictures that differ only slightly. In a cinema film there are normally **24 pictures per second**. Our eyes and brain can no longer see the fast pictures separately and perceive smooth movement. In the past the characters were drawn on transparent sheets, called **cels**, and laid on painted backgrounds. A long film needed hundreds of thousands of drawings.

In 1928 Walt Disney made Mickey Mouse famous with the film “Steamboat Willie”. In 1937 his first feature-length cartoon came out, **“Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs”**. Many people thought this was crazy, but the film was a huge success. Later came classics such as “The Jungle Book” from 1967 with Baloo the bear. In 1994 came **“The Lion King”** with the lion cub Simba, the meerkat Timon and the warthog Pumbaa.

In 1995 **“Toy Story”** was the first cinema film made entirely on the computer. It comes from the studio Pixar and tells of the cowboy Woody and the astronaut Buzz Lightyear. In this **computer animation** the characters are built as 3D models and moved digitally. Later came successes such as “Finding Nemo” (2003) about a clownfish and “Frozen” (2013) with the snowman Olaf. Today most big animated films are computer-animated.

abschnitte.titel: Animated films from around the world
abschnitte.text: It is not only America that makes animated films. In Japan cartoon films and series are called **anime**; a famous studio is Studio Ghibli, with “Spirited Away”. Maya the Bee comes from a book by the German writer Waldemar Bonsels from 1912. From 1975 she became famous as a cartoon series, and her best friend is the drone Willy. Besides drawn animation there is **stop-motion film**, in which figures made of modelling clay or wood are moved picture by picture.

The international animation festival **Fantoche** takes place in Baden every year. The director Claude Barras from Valais made the puppet animation film “My Life as a Courgette”, which was nominated for an Oscar in 2017. You can study animation at the Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts. Today many adverts and explainer videos are also made as animations.

begriffe.erklaerung: A technique with which still pictures are brought to life.
A transparent sheet on which cartoon characters used to be painted.
Animated film created with 3D models on the computer.
An animated film or series from Japan.
Figures are moved and photographed picture by picture.

gewusst: For “Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs” Walt Disney received an honorary Oscar with one large and seven small statuettes.
A flip book works on the same principle as a cartoon.
For “Toy Story” the computer sometimes needed several hours for a single picture.

teile.einleitung: The general theory of relativity is Albert Einstein’s theory of gravity. It explains gravity not as an invisible force, but as a curving of space and time. Einstein presented its field equations in 1915, and it is still considered one of the most accurate theories in physics.
wichtigste: Albert Einstein presented the field equations of the general theory of relativity in 1915.
Heavy bodies such as the Sun curve space and time.
Light is bent near large masses.
Near large masses, time passes more slowly.
The theory predicts black holes and gravitational waves.
Without it, the GPS system would not be accurate.

abschnitte.text: Isaac Newton described gravity as a **force** with which masses attract each other. Einstein saw it differently: mass bends **spacetime**, that is space and time together. You can imagine a stretched sheet with a heavy ball placed on it. If a small marble rolls past, it curves round the ball because of the dip. In the same way the planets circle the Sun.

Einstein worked on this theory for about ten years. For it he needed difficult mathematics, which his friend from his student days, **Marcel Grossmann** from Zurich, explained to him. In November 1915 he presented the **field equations** in Berlin. With them he was immediately able to solve an old puzzle: the small deviation in the orbit of the planet Mercury. Newton had not been able to explain this deviation.

The theory predicted that light from stars passing close to the Sun would be bent. During a **solar eclipse** in 1919, researchers led by Arthur Eddington were able to measure this. The stars really did appear to be shifted, exactly as Einstein had calculated. After that Einstein became world famous overnight. Today such **gravitational lenses** can often be seen in photos from telescopes.

The theory predicts **black holes**, from which not even light can escape. In 2019 the first image of a black hole was published. **Gravitational waves**, tiny ripples in spacetime, also follow from the theory. They were measured for the first time in 2015, exactly 100 years after Einstein’s work. The theory also explains that the universe is expanding.

Close to a large mass, time passes more slowly than further away. That is why clocks on a high mountain run very, very slightly faster than in the valley. Because of this, the clocks in **GPS satellites** differ each day by a few millionths of a second from clocks on Earth. Without correction, the location on your phone would be many kilometres out after just one day. So a theory from 1915 helps people find their way every day.

begriffe.erklaerung: Space and time together as a four-dimensional structure.
Another word for gravity.
A large mass that bends light like a magnifying glass.
A place with gravity so strong that nothing can escape.
A tiny wave that spreads through spacetime.

gewusst: Einstein himself long believed that gravitational waves could never be measured.
Because of the theory of relativity, someone who lives on a mountain ages very slightly faster than someone in the valley.
Marcel Grossmann, who helped Einstein with the mathematics, was a professor at ETH Zurich.

teile.einleitung: Directing is the artistic leadership of a film, a play or a television programme. The director decides how a story is told, how the actors perform and what the camera shows. Without a director, many separate shots would never become an exciting film.
wichtigste: The director gives artistic leadership to the actors, the camera and the whole film crew.
Alfred Hitchcock explained suspense with the example of a bomb under the table.
The 180-degree rule helps the audience to keep their bearings in a scene.
In “Rashomon” (1950) Akira Kurosawa showed one event from several points of view.
In 1968 Stanley Kubrick made “2001: A Space Odyssey”.
In 2010 Kathryn Bigelow became the first woman to win the Oscar for best director.
The Swiss director Xavier Koller won an Oscar in 1991 with “Journey of Hope”.

abschnitte.text: The director is in **artistic charge** of a film. They work with the screenplay and think about what each scene should look like. They often choose the actors and rehearse with them. During shooting they say when it is “Action” and when it is “Cut”. After the shoot they decide together with the **editor** which shots go into the finished film.

With shot sizes such as the long shot or the close-up, the director guides where you look. The **180-degree rule** says that during a conversation the camera should stay on one side of an imaginary line. Otherwise the characters seem to jump back and forth and you lose your bearings. Alfred Hitchcock explained **suspense** with a bomb under the table: if the audience knows about it but the characters do not, every second becomes tense. If it explodes without warning, it is only a short surprise.

In 1950 Akira Kurosawa from Japan made “Rashomon”, which shows the same event from contradictory points of view. In 1968 Stanley Kubrick created one of the best-known science fiction films, “2001: A Space Odyssey”. Jean-Luc Godard, a French-Swiss director, shaped the **Nouvelle Vague** and used striking jump cuts in “Breathless” (1960). In Denmark in 1995 Lars von Trier and Thomas Vinterberg founded the movement **Dogme 95**. Its rules banned, for example, special lighting and music added afterwards.

For a long time film directing was almost entirely a man's job. In 2010 Kathryn Bigelow became the first woman to win the **Oscar** for best director, for the war film “The Hurt Locker”. Since then Chloé Zhao and Jane Campion have also won this award. Today many film festivals and funding bodies are calling for more equality behind the camera.

In 1991 Xavier Koller won the **Oscar** for best foreign-language film with “Journey of Hope”. Marc Forster, who grew up in Davos, made the James Bond film “Quantum of Solace” in 2008. Important Swiss film festivals are the Locarno Film Festival and the Solothurn Film Festival. In Switzerland you can study directing, for example, at the Zurich University of the Arts, at ECAL in Lausanne or at HEAD in Geneva.

begriffe.erklaerung: The artistic leadership of a film or play.
Tension because the audience knows more than the characters.
During a conversation the camera stays on one side of the characters.
A visible jump in the picture because a piece has been cut out.
A French film movement around 1960 with new, free ideas.

gewusst: Alfred Hitchcock appeared very briefly as an extra in many of his own films.
The rules of Dogme 95 also required filming with a hand-held camera.
Stanley Kubrick filmed some scenes dozens of times until he was satisfied.

teile.einleitung: DanceSport is dancing as a competition. Couples perform standard and Latin dances, and there are also modern forms such as breaking and acrobatic disciplines. Technique, rhythm and expression are judged.
wichtigste: There are five standard dances and five Latin dances.
The Viennese waltz is danced in three-four time.
The jive is one of the Latin dances.
The paso doble is reminiscent of the Spanish bullfight.
Breaking began in New York in the 1970s and was an Olympic sport for the first time in Paris in 2024.
The world federation WDSF has its headquarters in Lausanne.

abschnitte.text: The five **standard dances** are the slow waltz, tango, **Viennese waltz**, slow foxtrot and quickstep. The couples hold each other in a fixed **dance hold** and move elegantly across the floor. Like all waltzes, the Viennese waltz is danced in **three-four time**, but it is much faster than the slow waltz.

The **Latin dances** include the samba, cha-cha-cha, rumba, **paso doble** and **jive**. They are rhythmic and full of temperament. In the paso doble the man plays the bullfighter and the woman his cape, the **capa**. The music is reminiscent of Spanish march music. Couples who dance all ten dances compete in the **ten-dance combination**.

**Breaking** began in the 1970s in the hip-hop culture of the **Bronx** in New York. The dancers are called **B-girls** and **B-boys**. They show fast steps, spins on the floor and powerful moves, often in a duel called a battle. In **Paris** in 2024 breaking was an Olympic sport for the first time. It is no longer included in the programme for Los Angeles 2028.

In **acrobatic rock 'n' roll** couples dance with fast footwork and show spectacular throws and flips. This sport is organised by the world federation WRRC. The world federation for standard, Latin and breaking is the **World DanceSport Federation (WDSF)**. It is recognised by the IOC and, like many other sports federations, has its headquarters in **Lausanne**.

gewusst: In DanceSport the couples are assessed by judges, much as in figure skating.
In the 19th century the Viennese waltz was a hugely fashionable dance in Vienna.

teile.einleitung: Gymnastics is a varied sport in which you train strength, flexibility, balance and courage. You do gymnastics on the floor, on apparatus such as the parallel bars and the horizontal bar, or jump on the trampoline. In Switzerland gymnastics has a long tradition; almost every village has a gymnastics club.
wichtigste: In a forward roll you roll forwards on the floor.
In a handstand you stand on your hands and stretch your legs upwards.
In a cartwheel you turn sideways over your hands like a wheel.
The parallel bars have two bars of the same height side by side.
Gymnasts balance on the narrow balance beam.
On the trampoline you jump high into the air on a stretched sheet.
The Federal Gymnastics Festival takes place every six years.

abschnitte.text: One of the first exercises is the **forward roll**, in which you roll forwards with a rounded back. In a **handstand** you stand on your hands and stretch your legs straight up. In a **cartwheel** you turn sideways over your hands like a wheel. Later come handsprings and somersaults. In competitions the floor exercises are combined into a free routine with music.

Men compete on six pieces of apparatus: floor, pommel horse, rings, vault, **parallel bars** and horizontal bar. The parallel bars have two bars of the same height side by side. Women compete on four pieces of apparatus: vault, uneven bars, **balance beam** and floor. The balance beam is only 10 centimetres wide, so you need very good balance.

Soft **mats** are placed under the apparatus so that you land safely. For difficult exercises a person helps by spotting; this is called giving support. On the **trampoline** you jump high into the air on a stretched sheet. Trampolining has even been an Olympic sport since 2000.

The Swiss Gymnastics Federation is one of the largest sports federations in the country. Every six years the **Federal Gymnastics Festival** takes place, with tens of thousands of gymnasts. The first was held in Aarau in 1832, and in 2025 Lausanne was the host. Club competitions with gymnastics, apparatus work and athletics are popular there.

Modern gymnastics goes back to the German **Friedrich Ludwig Jahn**, who is called the “father of gymnastics”. In 1811 he set up one of the first gymnastics grounds in Berlin. The Swiss gymnast Donghua Li became Olympic champion on the pommel horse in 1996. Giulia Steingruber won Olympic bronze on the vault in Rio in 2016.

begriffe.erklaerung: A piece of apparatus with two parallel rails.
A narrow, raised beam for balancing on.
An exercise put together by the gymnast, often with music.
Securing and supporting a person doing gymnastics.

gewusst: On the balance beam a gymnast lands somersaults on a surface that is narrower than the length of a palm.
Gymnastics has been on the programme since the first modern Olympic Games in 1896.
More athletes take part in the Federal Gymnastics Festival than in the Olympic Games.

teile.einleitung: Ice hockey is a fast team sport on ice in which two teams try to shoot a black rubber disc into the opponents' goal. The players skate on ice skates and play with sticks. In Switzerland ice hockey is one of the most popular sports of all.
wichtigste: The black disc in ice hockey is called a puck.
Each team has six players including the goalkeeper on the ice at the same time.
A game consists of three periods of 20 minutes each.
Anyone who gets a penalty has to go to the penalty box.
Ice hockey players wear skates and a lot of protective equipment.
The top league in Switzerland is called the National League.
Ice hockey originally comes from Canada.

abschnitte.text: Each team has five skaters and a **goalkeeper** on the ice. With a curved **stick** the **puck** is carried, passed and shot at goal. A game lasts three periods of 20 minutes of actual playing time each. Because ice hockey is very tiring, players often change after just one minute. If the score is level at the end, depending on the competition there is overtime and a penalty shootout.

The puck is a disc of hard rubber, about 7.6 centimetres wide and 2.5 centimetres thick. With hard shots it flies faster than 150 kilometres per hour. That is why the players wear a helmet, gloves and shoulder, elbow and shin pads. The goalkeeper has especially thick padding and a mask. On their feet everyone wears **ice skates** with sharp blades.

Body contact is allowed in men's ice hockey, but only under clear rules. Anyone who hooks an opponent with the stick, holds them or attacks them dangerously usually has to go to the **penalty box** for two minutes. Their team then plays with one player fewer; this is called being **short-handed**. For serious offences there are longer penalties or a game misconduct (being sent off).

Modern ice hockey developed in the 19th century in **Canada**; in 1875 an early indoor game took place in Montreal. Ice hockey has been an Olympic sport since 1920. The North American **NHL** is regarded as the strongest league in the world. Canada, the USA, Sweden, Finland, the Czech Republic and Switzerland are among the strong ice hockey nations.

The top league in Switzerland is the **National League**, with clubs such as SC Bern, HC Davos and EV Zug. Every year between Christmas and New Year the **Spengler Cup** takes place in Davos, one of the oldest club tournaments in the world. The Swiss national team has won silver at the World Championships several times, including in 2013, 2018, 2024 and 2025. Swiss players such as Roman Josi and Nico Hischier are stars in the NHL.

begriffe.erklaerung: The black hard rubber disc with which ice hockey is played.
One of the three parts of the game, each lasting 20 minutes.
The bench where a penalised player has to wait.
When a team plays with fewer players because of a penalty.
The National Hockey League, the most famous professional league in North America.

gewusst: Before every game the pucks are often chilled so that they bounce less.
The Spengler Cup in Davos has been held since 1923.
In 2017 Nico Hischier became the first Swiss player ever to be picked first in the NHL draft.

teile.einleitung: A comic tells a story with a sequence of pictures in which the characters talk in speech bubbles. Pictures and text work together, so that you read along almost as if you were watching a film. From Asterix and Mickey Mouse to Globi, children and adults all over the world love comics.
wichtigste: A comic is a story told in a series of drawn pictures.
What the characters say is written in speech bubbles, what they think often in thought bubbles.
Rodolphe Töpffer from Geneva is regarded as one of the inventors of the picture story.
Famous comics from France and Belgium are Asterix, Tintin, Lucky Luke and the Smurfs.
Characters such as Mickey Mouse, Donald Duck, Superman and Garfield come from the USA.
In Japan comics are called manga and are read from right to left.
The best-known Swiss comic character is the blue parrot Globi.

abschnitte.text: A comic consists of many single pictures, the **panels**, which you read in order. What the characters say is written in **speech bubbles**, and noises such as “Boom” or “Pow” are drawn as big sound words. Between two pictures something often happens that you have to imagine yourself. In this way a flowing story forms in your head. Short comics in newspapers are called **comic strips**; they often have only three or four pictures.

Almost 200 years ago the Geneva teacher **Rodolphe Töpffer** was already drawing funny picture stories with text under the pictures. In 1865 “Max and Moritz” by **Wilhelm Busch** was published in Germany. In the USA comics became popular in newspapers around 1900, and from the 1930s also in their own magazines. In 1938 Superman appeared, the first big superhero. Since then comics have been a huge part of entertainment.

France and Belgium are famous for their comics, which are called **bandes dessinées** there. Asterix and Obelix were invented in 1959 by René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo. The Gauls become strong thanks to a **magic potion**; only Obelix is not allowed any, because he fell into it as a baby, and his little dog is called Dogmatix. In 1929 the Belgian **Hergé** invented the reporter Tintin and his dog Snowy. Lucky Luke with his horse Jolly Jumper and the blue Smurfs also come from Belgium.

abschnitte.titel: Comics from the USA and Japan
abschnitte.text: In the USA Walt Disney's characters such as Mickey Mouse and Donald Duck with his nephews **Huey, Dewey and Louie** became world-famous. The lazy cat **Garfield** loves lasagne and has appeared in newspapers since 1978. Superheroes such as Spider-Man or Batman come from big comic publishers such as Marvel and DC. In Japan **manga** are very popular, for example “One Piece” or “Dragon Ball”. Manga are usually black and white and are read from back to front.

The best-known Swiss comic character is **Globi**, a blue parrot with trousers and a cap. He was invented in 1932 as an advertising figure for the Globus department store and has had adventures in many books ever since. The Swiss artist Derib created the Native American boy Yakari, who can talk to animals. Every year the comic festival Fumetto takes place in **Lucerne**. Töpffer from Geneva also shows that Switzerland plays an important role in the history of comics.

First someone writes the story and plans what happens on each page. Then an artist draws sketches in pencil. After that the lines are inked and the pictures are **coloured**, today often on the computer. Finally the text goes into the speech bubbles. Long comics for adults with serious themes are called **graphic novels**.

begriffe.erklaerung: A single picture in a comic, usually with a frame.
A bubble with a pointed tail that shows what a character says.
The name for comics from Japan.
Words that sound like a noise, for example “Whoomp” or “Splash”.
A long comic that tells a whole story like a novel.

gewusst: The Asterix books have been translated into over a hundred languages and dialects, even into Latin and Bernese German.
Hergé's real name was Georges Remi; his reversed initials R. G. became his pen name.
Globi wears black and red checked trousers and a beret.

teile.einleitung: A video game genre is a group of video games that work in a similar way and have a similar aim. Whether you jump over platforms, race, build cities or solve puzzles, there is a genre for almost everything. Genres help you find the right game.
wichtigste: A genre groups together games with similar gameplay.
In a platformer (jump 'n' run) the character jumps over platforms and obstacles, as in Super Mario.
Mario Kart is a racing game, Tetris a puzzle game.
RPG stands for role-playing game.
In city-building games such as SimCity you plan and manage a city.
Open-world games have a large world that you can explore freely.
In turn-based strategy games the players take turns; in real-time strategy they act at the same time.
Many modern games mix several genres.

abschnitte.text: The word **genre** comes from French and means kind or type. Games belong to the same genre if you do similar things in them, for example jumping, fighting, building or solving puzzles. Books, films and music also have genres. The division is not always exact, because many games are **hybrids**. Nevertheless, genres help when describing and choosing games.

In a **platformer** (jump 'n' run) you steer a character through levels and jump over chasms and enemies; the best-known example is “Super Mario Bros.” from 1985. In a **racing game** you race against others, for example in “Mario Kart” or in realistic car simulations. **Sports games** recreate sports such as football or ice hockey. In a **rhythm game** you press buttons in time to the music or dance, as in “Just Dance”. Here quick reactions and good coordination count.

In **puzzle games** such as “Tetris” you have to arrange falling blocks cleverly so that full rows disappear. In a **point-and-click adventure** you click on objects with the mouse, collect them, combine them and talk to characters to solve puzzles. A well-known example is the pirate series “Monkey Island”. **Educational games** are meant to teach knowledge, for example in maths or when learning vocabulary. Games like these encourage logical thinking and patience.

In **city-building games** such as “SimCity” you plan a city with roads, houses and power stations. In **strategy games** you lead a people or an army and have to plan cleverly. In **turn-based** games such as “Civilization” the players take turns, as in chess. In **real-time strategy** such as “Age of Empires” time keeps running for everyone at once. **Simulations** imitate real activities, such as flying or working on a farm.

In a **role-playing game**, RPG for short, you take on the role of a character who becomes stronger and learns new skills. Well-known examples are the “Pokémon” games or “Final Fantasy”. **Open-world games** have a huge world without a fixed path that you may explore freely, as in “The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild”. “Minecraft” also has an open world in which you can build almost anything. **Action-adventures** combine fighting with exploring and puzzles.

Not every genre is suitable for every age. In **shooters** you shoot at enemies, and many of them are only rated for ages 16 or 18. In Switzerland and large parts of Europe the **PEGI rating** on the packaging shows from what age a game is suitable. Puzzle, racing and platform games, on the other hand, are often rated for children from 3 or 7. In this way parents and children can choose suitable games together.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of games, films or books that are similar to each other.
Short for role-playing game, a game in which your own character develops.
A large, open game world that you can explore freely.
The game keeps running without pause, and everyone acts at the same time.
A European system that gives the age rating of games.

gewusst: Tetris was invented in Moscow in 1984 by Alexey Pajitnov and is one of the best-selling games in the world.
The well-known “Farming Simulator” comes from the company Giants Software, which is based in Switzerland.
The expression jump 'n' run is English and means “jump and run”.

teile.einleitung: Game design is designing games: their rules, goals, worlds and challenges. Game designers think about what makes a game exciting and how it should feel. In doing so they use knowledge from psychology, mathematics, art and storytelling.
wichtigste: Game design decides the rules, goals and sequences of a game.
The core loop is the central sequence of actions that keeps repeating.
The MDA model stands for mechanics, dynamics, aesthetics.
The right level of difficulty is meant to trigger “flow” as described by Mihály Csíkszentmihályi.
Richard Bartle divided players into types, such as the explorer, who likes to explore the world.
In procedural generation, algorithms create game content such as landscapes.
An item with a 5 per cent chance appears at least once in two attempts with a probability of 9.75 per cent.
Testing with real players is an important part of game design.

abschnitte.text: **Game design** is planning a game, whether a board game or a video game. Game designers decide which rules apply, what the goal is and what decisions the players can make. They work closely with programmers, artists, musicians and writers. An important tool is the **prototype**, a simple first version that can be tried out quickly. This way you find out early on whether an idea is really fun.

The **core loop** is the central sequence of actions that you carry out again and again. In Minecraft, for example, it is: collect resources, build things, survive dangers. The **MDA model** describes games on three levels: mechanics are the rules, dynamics the behaviour that results from them during play, and aesthetics the players' feelings. Designers build mechanics so that a particular feeling arises in the end, such as suspense or the joy of discovery. The model was presented in 2004 by three game developers.

The psychologist **Mihály Csíkszentmihályi** described **flow**, a state in which you are completely absorbed in an activity and forget the time. It arises when a task is neither too easy nor too difficult. If a game is too easy, it becomes boring; if it is too hard, you get frustrated. Some games adjust the difficulty automatically to your performance; this is called **dynamic difficulty adjustment**. Fine-tuning strengths and weaknesses is called balancing.

In 1996 the British researcher **Richard Bartle** divided players of online games into four types. **Achievers** want to collect points and successes, while **explorers** like best to explore the game world and its secrets. **Socialisers** play mainly to be with others. Killers want to compete with others and win. Good games offer something for several types.

In **procedural generation** an algorithm creates landscapes, caves or levels automatically instead of by hand. This is typical of **roguelikes**, in which the levels are created randomly and the character is lost for good if defeated. Probabilities also play a role. If an item has a 5 per cent chance on each attempt, you get it at least once in two attempts with a probability of 1 minus 0.95 times 0.95, that is 9.75 per cent. Designers calculate such values so that a game feels fair.

Many games tell a story; this is called **narrative design**. If the story and the game mechanics do not fit together, it is called **ludonarrative dissonance**. An example would be a friendly heroine who, in the game, is mainly rewarded for defeating lots of enemies. In Switzerland you can study game design at the Zurich University of the Arts. Swiss studios develop games for consoles, computers and smartphones.

begriffe.erklaerung: The central sequence of actions that keeps repeating in the game.
A first, simple version of a game for trying out.
A state in which you are completely absorbed in a task.
Fine-tuning a game so that it stays fair and exciting.
An exact step-by-step set of instructions that a computer carries out.

gewusst: The roguelike genre is named after the computer game “Rogue” from 1980.
The world of Minecraft is generated procedurally and is almost infinitely large.
The word “ludo” comes from Latin and means “I play”.

teile.einleitung: Endurance is the ability to keep up an effort for a long time without getting tired quickly. You need it for running, cycling, swimming or cross-country skiing, but also in everyday life. If you train regularly, you strengthen your heart, lungs and muscles.
wichtigste: Endurance means being able to keep up an effort for a long time.
In aerobic energy production the muscle gets enough oxygen.
During very intense effort without enough oxygen, lactate builds up in the muscle.
The red blood cells carry oxygen to the muscles.
Endurance training makes the heart pump more blood with each beat.
A marathon is 42.195 kilometres long, a half marathon 21.0975 kilometres.
In a triathlon you swim, cycle and run one after the other.

abschnitte.text: **Endurance** is the body's ability to resist tiredness for a long time and then recover quickly. Together with strength, speed, flexibility and coordination, it is one of the most important sporting abilities. Experts distinguish **basic endurance** for long, steady efforts from endurance for fast, hard efforts. Typical endurance sports are running, cycling, swimming, rowing and cross-country skiing.

Muscles need energy, which they get from sugar and fat. If they get enough oxygen while doing so, this is called **aerobic** energy production, and you can keep going for a long time. During very intense effort the oxygen is no longer enough, and then the muscle works **anaerobically**. This produces **lactate**, and you quickly get tired and have to slow down. The red blood cells carry the oxygen from the lungs to the muscles.

If you train your endurance regularly, your body changes. The **heart** becomes stronger and pumps more blood with each beat, which is why your resting pulse goes down. The muscles form more of the tiny power stations in their cells, the mitochondria. Your immune system, your mood and your sleep also benefit. For children and teenagers the World Health Organization recommends at least one hour of exercise a day.

The **marathon** over 42.195 kilometres goes back to a legend from ancient Greece. In a **triathlon** you swim first, then cycle and finally run. In Switzerland the Engadin Skimarathon and the Jungfrau Marathon are well known; the latter starts in Interlaken and leads high up into the mountains. The Tour de France demands endurance from professional cyclists for three weeks.

Endurance is best trained at a steady pace at which you can still talk. It is better to train often and regularly than rarely and very hard. Before training you warm up, and afterwards you drink enough water. Cycling to school, swimming or playing football with friends also improves your endurance.

begriffe.erklaerung: With enough oxygen, so the muscle can work for a long time.
Without enough oxygen; the muscle then tires quickly.
A substance that builds up in the muscle during very hard effort.
The number of heartbeats per minute.
A competition made up of swimming, cycling and running in that order.

gewusst: In well-trained endurance athletes the heart often beats only about 40 times a minute at rest.
The strange marathon distance of 42.195 kilometres was fixed at the 1908 Olympic Games in London.
Humans are among the best long-distance runners in the whole animal kingdom.

teile.einleitung: A children's book is a book written especially for children and often lovingly illustrated. From picture books for the very youngest to exciting novels for schoolchildren, there are countless kinds. Characters such as Heidi, Pippi Longstocking or the Very Hungry Caterpillar are known all over the world.
wichtigste: Children's books range from picture books to children's novels.
Astrid Lindgren wrote the books about Pippi Longstocking, whose monkey is called Mr Nilsson.
The Swiss writer Johanna Spyri wrote “Heidi”.
Heidi lives with her grandfather on an Alpine pasture, and her friend Clara uses a wheelchair.
Ursli wants a big bell for Chalandamarz.
The Very Hungry Caterpillar becomes a butterfly at the end.
The Rainbow Fish by the Swiss author Marcus Pfister gives away his glittering scales.

abschnitte.text: A **children's book** is written for young readers, with language and length to suit their age. For the very youngest there are **picture books**, in which the pictures help to tell the story. Later come early readers with large print and short sentences. For older children there are **children's novels**, non-fiction books and comics. Children's books bring the joy of reading and stimulate the imagination.

**Johanna Spyri** from Zurich wrote the two books about **Heidi** in 1880 and 1881. Heidi lives with her grandfather, the Alm-Uncle (Alpöhi), on an Alpine pasture in the mountains of the Grisons and is later sent to Frankfurt. There she makes friends with Clara, who uses a wheelchair. “**A Bell for Ursli**” (Schellen-Ursli) by Selina Chönz with pictures by Alois Carigiet came out in 1945. Ursli from the Engadine wants a big bell for the procession at Chalandamarz.

The Swede **Astrid Lindgren** is one of the most famous children's authors in the world. In 1945 her first book about **Pippi Longstocking**, the strongest girl in the world, came out. Pippi lives in Villa Villekulla with her monkey Mr Nilsson and her horse. Lindgren also wrote “Emil of Lönneberga”, “Ronia, the Robber's Daughter” and “The Children of Noisy Village”. Her books have been translated into over a hundred languages.

In “The Very Hungry Caterpillar” by Eric Carle from 1969 a caterpillar eats its way through the week and at the end becomes a **butterfly**. In 1992 the Swiss author **Marcus Pfister** created “The Rainbow Fish”, who gives his glittering scales away to other fish and so finds friends. In “**The Gruffalo**” by Julia Donaldson and Axel Scheffler a little mouse invents a monster to protect itself from predators. Books like these are often read aloud. Many of them have also been published in Swiss German.

In 1960 **Michael Ende** wrote “Jim Button and Luke the Engine Driver”; the two friends' locomotive is called Emma. He also wrote “The Neverending Story”. Other classics are “Lottie and Lisa” by Erich Kästner and “Harry Potter” by J. K. Rowling. As early as 1845 “**Struwwelpeter**” (Shockheaded Peter) by Heinrich Hoffmann came out, one of the first well-known German picture books. Many children's books were later made into films.

Since 1931 the **Swiss Youth Literature Foundation** (SJW) has published cheap booklets for children. Schools and libraries promote reading with events such as the Swiss Reading Aloud Day. In Switzerland children's books are published in German, French, Italian and Romansh. An important international award is the **Hans Christian Andersen Award**, named after the Danish writer of fairy tales. Good children's books are often passed down through generations.

begriffe.erklaerung: A book for small children in which the pictures tell the story.
A picture that goes with a text and explains it.
A longer story in chapters for schoolchildren.
A spring custom in the Grisons on 1 March in which children drive away winter with bells.

gewusst: “Heidi” is one of the most translated books in Swiss literature.
The idea for Pippi Longstocking came about when Astrid Lindgren's sick daughter asked for stories about a girl with that name.
In “The Very Hungry Caterpillar” many pages have real holes that you can poke your finger through.

teile.einleitung: In apparatus gymnastics you do exercises on various pieces of equipment in the gym. You climb, jump, hang and balance. In top-level sport it is called artistic gymnastics and is part of the Olympic Games.
wichtigste: On the wall bars you can climb and hold on.
The vaulting box consists of several parts that are stacked on top of each other.
The springboard helps you take off over the box or the buck.
On the horizontal bar you work on a single bar, on the rings on two ropes.
In artistic gymnastics men compete on six pieces of apparatus, women on four.

abschnitte.text: The **wall bars** consist of many horizontal wooden bars on the wall. You can climb them and do exercises. The **gym bench** is a long, narrow wooden bench. You can sit on it, balance on it or turn it upside down, which makes balancing harder. Other climbing equipment includes ropes and poles.

The **vaulting box** consists of several wooden frames and a padded top. If you take parts away, it becomes lower. The **buck** has four legs and a pad on top. You jump over it with the help of your hands, for example with a straddle. The **springboard** springs back when you take off and helps you jump higher.

The **horizontal bar** is a horizontal metal bar. You can hang from it, swing or pull yourself up. The **rings** hang from the ceiling on two ropes. Mats provide safety. The **crash mat** is particularly thick and soft and catches you gently when you jump from a great height.

In **artistic gymnastics** men compete on **six pieces of apparatus**: floor, pommel horse, rings, vault, parallel bars and horizontal bar. Women compete on **four pieces of apparatus**: vault, uneven bars, balance beam and floor. So **floor** and **vault** exist for both. Only men compete on the **rings**, and only women on the **balance beam**. In Switzerland the gymnastics federation is one of the largest sports federations.

gewusst: The balance beam is only about 10 centimetres wide.
Gymnastics clubs have a long tradition in Switzerland; many municipalities have their own gymnastics club.

teile.einleitung: Handball is a fast team game in which you throw and catch the ball with your hands. The aim is to throw the ball into the opponents' goal. In Switzerland handball is played in many clubs.
wichtigste: Each team has seven people on the court: six court players and one goalkeeper.
For adults a match lasts two times 30 minutes.
You may hold the ball for at most three seconds.
The goal area reaches six metres out in front of the goal.
The penalty throw is taken from seven metres.
A suspension lasts two minutes.

abschnitte.text: In **indoor handball** two teams play against each other. Each team has **six court players** and **one goalkeeper** on the court, seven in total. You pass the ball to each other and try to score a **goal**. Players may be substituted as often as you like during the match. For adults a match lasts **two times 30 minutes** with a break in between.

You may hold the ball in your hand for at most **three seconds**, even if you are standing still. With the ball in your hand you may take at most **three steps**. After that you have to bounce it, pass or shoot. This keeps the game fast. You may not play the ball with your feet, except for the goalkeeper when defending.

In front of each goal is the **goal area**; it reaches **6 metres** out. Nobody except the goalkeeper may enter it. But players often jump high and throw before they land in the goal area. If a clear chance to score is stopped illegally, there is a **penalty throw**. Because it is taken from **7 metres**, it is also called a **seven-metre throw**.

For minor fouls there is a free throw. For more serious offences the referee shows a **yellow card** as a warning. After that comes a **suspension**: the player has to leave the court for **2 minutes**. During this time their team plays with one player fewer. After three suspensions or for serious fouls there is a **red card**.

gewusst: In the past handball was also played outdoors on large grass pitches with eleven players per team.
The handball is rubbed with resin so that it is easier to grip.

teile.einleitung: Strength training is training in which the muscles work against a resistance, for example against weights or your own body weight. It makes you stronger, protects against injuries and helps in almost every sport. Done properly, it is healthy for children and teenagers too.
wichtigste: In strength training the muscles work against a resistance.
Maximum strength is the greatest force a muscle can produce at will.
Explosive strength is the ability to develop force as quickly as possible, for example when taking off.
Many repetitions with a light weight mainly train strength endurance.
The biceps bends the arm at the elbow joint.
In a forearm plank you hold a position; this is an isometric exercise.
Children should first train with their own body weight.

abschnitte.text: In **strength training** the muscles have to work against a resistance. This can be a dumbbell, a resistance band, a machine in the gym or simply your own body weight. The body responds by making the muscles stronger and often bigger too. Bones, tendons and joints also become more robust.

Experts distinguish several kinds of strength. **Maximum strength** is the greatest force a muscle can produce at will, important for example in weightlifting. You need **explosive strength** for fast movements, such as taking off or throwing. **Strength endurance** lets you keep going for many repetitions, for example in rowing or climbing.

Humans have over 600 muscles. The **biceps** on the upper arm bends the arm, and its opposing muscle, the triceps, straightens it. **Squats** mainly train the leg muscles, press-ups the chest, shoulders and arms. In a forearm plank you hold a position without moving; this is called an isometric exercise. It particularly strengthens the core muscles of the stomach and back.

**Weightlifting** is an Olympic sport in which you lift a barbell that is as heavy as possible. There are two events: the **snatch**, in which the bar is pulled up over the head in one movement, and the **clean and jerk**, in which it is first lifted onto the shoulders and then pushed upwards. Powerlifting and bodybuilding are related. Top athletes lift more than twice their own body weight.

Children and teenagers should first train with their **own body weight**, for example with press-ups, pull-ups or squats. This way they learn the correct technique and do not overload their joints. Heavy weights only belong in training later and only under supervision. Clean technique, warming up and enough rest are important, because muscles grow during recovery. The World Health Organization recommends that children also strengthen their muscles and bones on at least three days a week.

begriffe.erklaerung: The greatest force a muscle can produce at will.
The ability to develop a lot of force in a short time.
The ability to keep up many strength movements one after the other.
An exercise in which the muscle works without you moving.
Pain in the muscle one or two days after unaccustomed effort.

gewusst: Muscles do not grow during training but in the rest periods afterwards.
The largest muscle in the human body is the gluteus maximus in the buttocks.
Muscles can only pull, not push, which is why they always work in pairs, as a muscle and its opposing muscle.

teile.einleitung: Game development is the work in which an idea becomes a finished video game. Programmers, designers, artists, musicians and testers work together on it. Big games sometimes need hundreds of people and several years of work.
wichtigste: A game engine is a software framework for graphics, physics and game logic.
At 60 frames per second only about 16.7 milliseconds of computing time are left for each frame.
The finished version for copying is called the gold master.
Crunch is a criticised phase with lots of overtime before release.
Many teams work in an agile way with Scrum, in fixed cycles called sprints.
In 1972 Pong made arcade video games a mass success for the first time.
Tetris was created in the Soviet Union in 1984.

abschnitte.text: It all starts with an idea, which is worked out in detail in **game design**. The rules, goals, characters and levels are decided. Then the team builds a simple **prototype** to test whether the game is fun. In production the graphics, music, program code and story are created. At the end testers look for errors, known as bugs.

Most games are built with a **game engine**, such as Unity or the Unreal Engine. It takes care of graphics, physics, sound and game logic, so that not everything has to be programmed from scratch. If a game is to run at 60 frames per second, only about 16.7 milliseconds are left for each frame. For hits and collisions the game uses invisible, simple shapes, the **hitboxes**. With **ray tracing**, modern graphics cards calculate the path of light rays for realistic reflections.

Programmers write the code, artists draw characters and landscapes, and sound designers make noises and music. Game designers think up rules and levels. Producers plan time and money. Many teams work with the agile method **Scrum**, in which work is done in sprints usually lasting one to four weeks. Shortly before release there is often the controversial **crunch** with a great deal of overtime.

In 1972 the company Atari brought the game **Pong** to amusement arcades, the first big hit game. In 1984 Alexey Pajitnov programmed the game **Tetris** in Moscow, then in the Soviet Union. In the past a few people could develop a whole game. Today big titles often cost as much as a Hollywood film. There are also many small **indie studios** that make creative games with little money.

In Switzerland there are numerous small game studios, especially in Zurich, Geneva and Lausanne. You can study game design, for example, at the **Zurich University of the Arts**. The cultural foundation Pro Helvetia supports Swiss games and takes them to international trade fairs. When a game is finished, the **gold master** is approved, that is the version that is copied or released. Today updates over the internet often follow afterwards.

begriffe.erklaerung: A software framework with which games are built.
A first, simple test version of a game.
An error in a program.
An invisible shape with which a game calculates hits.
A period with a great deal of overtime before a game is launched.

gewusst: The name gold master comes from the gold-coloured CDs on which the finished version used to be burned.
Tetris first spread secretly on floppy disks from computer to computer in the Soviet Union.
Some games have deliberately kept funny bugs because the players liked them.

teile.einleitung: Ball games are among the most popular games at school and in clubs. They are usually played in teams and need skill, speed and teamwork. Every ball game has its own rules.
wichtigste: In dodgeball you hit your opponents with the ball.
In Brennball you run around the bases after throwing the ball.
In football the team with more goals wins, and only the goalkeeper may use their hands.
In volleyball you play the ball over the net with your hands and arms.
In floorball (Unihockey) you hit the ball with a plastic stick.

abschnitte.text: In **dodgeball** each team tries to hit the players of the other team with the ball. Anyone who is hit has to go to the area behind the opponents and can keep throwing from there. In **Brennball**, a game similar to rounders, one player throws the ball into the field and then runs around the **bases**. The other team tries to get the ball to the “burning” base quickly. Anyone who is still on the way at that moment is “burnt”.

In **football** only the **goals** count: whoever has scored more at the end wins. Outfield players may not play the ball with their hands or arms. Only the **goalkeeper** may pick it up, inside their penalty area. If the ball goes over the touchline, there is a **throw-in** with both hands over the head. If a defender plays the ball over their own goal line, there is a **corner kick**, in Switzerland also just called a corner.

In **volleyball** two teams stand on either side of a high **net**. You play the ball with your hands and arms without catching it. The aim is for the ball to land on the ground in the opponents' court. Each team may touch the ball at most three times before it has to go over the net. In summer people often also play beach volleyball on sand.

In **Unihockey** every player has a plastic **stick**. With it you dribble, pass and shoot a light ball with holes. Unihockey is very popular in Switzerland and is played in many schools. There are many clubs and a national championship. Internationally the sport is called **floorball**.

gewusst: Switzerland is one of the strongest nations in the world at floorball.
FIFA, the world football federation, has its headquarters in Zurich.

teile.einleitung: Every person has their own voice, which sounds rather high or rather low. In music, singing voices are sorted into voice types. That way you know which notes a singer can sing comfortably.
wichtigste: The main female voices are soprano, mezzo-soprano and alto.
The main male voices are tenor, baritone and bass.
A mixed choir usually sings in four parts: soprano, alto, tenor, bass (SATB).
The vocal range goes from the lowest to the highest note a voice can sing.
A countertenor is a man who sings in the alto range using his head voice.
The contralto is the lowest female voice and is rather rare.

abschnitte.text: The **voice type** describes the range of notes in which a voice sounds best. Women and children usually sing higher than grown men because their vocal folds are shorter. The **vocal range** shows how many notes someone can reach. But tone colour is important too: a voice can sound bright, dark, light or powerful. Singing teachers help people to find the right voice type.

The **soprano** is the highest female voice. The **mezzo-soprano** lies in the middle, because “mezzo” means “half” or “middle” in Italian. Below that comes the **alto**, and lower still the rare **contralto**. A **coloratura soprano** is a particularly high and agile soprano. Coloratura means fast, decorated runs of notes, such as the Queen of the Night sings in Mozart's “The Magic Flute”.

The **tenor** is the high male voice, the **bass** the lowest. In between lies the **baritone**. The **bass-baritone** combines the depth of the bass with the height of the baritone. A **countertenor** sings as high as an alto voice with a well-trained head voice. This voice type is especially popular in Baroque music.

In a **mixed choir** women and men sing together. The abbreviation **SATB** stands for soprano, alto, tenor and bass, from the highest to the lowest voice. Each part sings its own melody, and together they create a full sound. In Switzerland many municipalities have church choirs, yodelling clubs and youth choirs. Children's choirs often sing in one or two parts.

gewusst: In boys the voice gets deeper during the teenage years. This is called the voice breaking.
The voice is produced in the larynx, where the vocal folds are set vibrating by the air we breathe out.

teile.einleitung: In music, tempo means the speed at which a piece is played. It is given with Italian words or with a number for the metronome. The tempo strongly changes the effect music has on us.
wichtigste: Adagio means slow, Andante calm and at a walking pace.
Allegro means fast and lively, Presto very fast.
Accelerando means gradually faster, ritardando gradually slower.
A metronome counts the beats per minute.
At 120 on the metronome it ticks every half second.
“Flight of the Bumblebee” by Rimsky-Korsakov is a famous, very fast piece.

abschnitte.text: Above the music there are usually **Italian** tempo words. **Adagio** means “at ease”, so you play slowly. **Andante** comes from the word for “to walk” and is calm like a leisurely stroll. **Allegro** actually means “cheerful” and stands for a fast, lively tempo. **Presto** means “quick” and is one of the fastest tempos.

A **metronome** is a device that ticks evenly. The number shows the **beats per minute**. At 60 it ticks every second, at 120 every half second. Johann Nepomuk Maelzel had the metronome patented in 1815. Today metronomes also exist as an app on your mobile phone, and when you practise they help you to play evenly.

The tempo does not always have to stay the same. In an **accelerando** the music gradually gets faster; the word means “speeding up”. In a **ritardando** it gradually gets slower, often at the end of a piece. This creates tension or a calm ending. Conductors show such changes with their movements.
