**“Flight of the Bumblebee”** is by the Russian composer **Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov**. It belongs to an opera in which a character turns into a bumblebee. The many fast notes sound like the buzzing of a flying bumblebee. Musicians like to play the piece to show how fast they are. It is played on the violin, piano, trumpet and many other instruments.

gewusst: The abbreviation “M.M.” in front of a tempo number means “Maelzel's metronome”.
A calm heartbeat in adults is roughly in the range of an Andante tempo.

teile.einleitung: Archimedes’ principle explains why a steel ship floats and why you feel lighter in water. It says that a body in water receives an upward force as large as the weight of the water it pushes aside. It was discovered by the Greek scholar Archimedes over 2200 years ago.
wichtigste: A body in a liquid or a gas experiences buoyancy.
The buoyancy is exactly as large as the weight of the liquid pushed aside.
If the body is lighter than the liquid pushed aside, it floats.
If it is heavier, it sinks to the bottom.
Archimedes of Syracuse lived from about 287 to 212 BC.
According to legend, he shouted “Eureka!” when he had the idea in the bath.
Ships, submarines and hot-air balloons work thanks to this principle.

abschnitte.text: Every body that dips into water pushes water aside. This displaced water pushes upwards with a force called **buoyancy**. The buoyancy is as large as the weight of the displaced water. So a stone with a volume of 1 litre displaces 1 litre of water and becomes about 1 kilogram lighter.

Archimedes lived in **Syracuse** on the island of Sicily. King Hiero II wanted to know whether his new crown was really made of pure gold. When Archimedes got into a full bath and water spilled over, he is said to have seen the solution. He supposedly ran naked through the town shouting **“Eureka!”**, which is Greek for “I have found it!”. Nobody knows for certain whether the story happened exactly like this.

A steel ship is mostly hollow inside and filled with air. Because of this it displaces a great deal of water, even though it is not so heavy overall. The ship sinks down until the displaced water weighs as much as the ship itself. The more heavily a cargo ship is loaded, the lower it lies in the water; this is shown by the **load line** on the hull.

The principle applies not only to water but also to gases such as air. A **hot-air balloon** rises because the warm air in the balloon is lighter than the cool air outside. Balloons filled with helium float for the same reason. A **submarine** pumps water into tanks to sink and pushes it out again with air to come up.

In the **Dead Sea** the water is so salty and heavy that people float on the surface almost by themselves. Fish control their depth with an air-filled **swim bladder**. A life jacket keeps you up because it displaces a lot of water and is itself very light. Ice floats too, because frozen water is a little lighter than liquid water.

begriffe.erklaerung: The force with which water or air pushes a body upwards.
The water that a body pushes aside when it dips in.
How heavy a substance is in relation to its size.
Greek for “I have found it!”.

gewusst: Only about a tenth of an iceberg sticks out of the water; most of it lies below.
Archimedes also invented a water screw that can lift water upwards.
The cry “Eureka” is today the motto of the US state of California.

teile.einleitung: Exercise physiology studies what happens in the body during sport. It explains where the muscles get their energy from, how the heart and lungs work and how the body changes through training. This knowledge helps coaches and athletes to train better and more healthily.
wichtigste: In short sprints the energy comes mainly from splitting creatine phosphate.
Type I fibres are slow-twitch, very enduring muscle fibres.
VO2max gives the maximum oxygen uptake per minute.
Cardiac output is stroke volume times heart rate.
In anaerobic glycolysis lactate is formed from pyruvate.
Aerobic energy production takes place in the mitochondria.
During muscle contraction actin and myosin slide past each other.

abschnitte.text: Muscles need the substance **ATP** as their direct source of energy, but only a little of it is stored. During maximum efforts of a few seconds, such as a 30-metre sprint, new ATP comes mainly from **splitting creatine phosphate**. After that, sugar is broken down without oxygen in anaerobic glycolysis. In this process **lactate** is formed from pyruvate. During long efforts the body produces energy with oxygen, in the mitochondria, through the citric acid cycle and the respiratory chain.

A muscle consists of many fibres. According to the **sliding filament theory**, during contraction the proteins **actin** and **myosin** slide past each other, and in this way the muscle shortens. Type I fibres twitch slowly but hardly tire and are important for endurance. Type II fibres are fast and powerful but quickly exhausted. Marathon runners usually have more type I fibres, sprinters more type II fibres.

**Cardiac output** tells you how much blood the heart pumps per minute. You calculate it as stroke volume times heart rate: 100 millilitres times 180 beats gives 18 litres per minute. At rest it is only about 5 litres. The maximum heart rate is estimated with the rule of thumb 220 minus your age, so 202 beats per minute at the age of 18. Long, intense endurance training can lead to an enlarged, healthy **athlete's heart**.

**VO2max** tells you the maximum amount of oxygen the body can take in per minute. It is an important measure of endurance. Top athletes in cross-country skiing or cycling have especially high values. It is measured in an exercise test with a breathing mask on a treadmill or a bike.

The body adapts to training: the muscles become stronger, the heart more powerful and more mitochondria are formed. During **altitude training** the kidney produces more of the hormone **erythropoietin**, EPO for short. As a result more red blood cells are produced, which carry oxygen. That is why many athletes train at high altitude, for example in St Moritz. Injecting artificial EPO, on the other hand, is banned doping.

begriffe.erklaerung: The energy carrier in every cell, the direct source of energy for muscles.
The salt of lactic acid, produced during effort without enough oxygen.
The power stations of the cell, in which energy is produced with oxygen.
The maximum amount of oxygen the body can take in per minute.
A hormone from the kidney that stimulates the production of red blood cells.

gewusst: An endurance athlete can have a resting pulse of under 40 beats per minute.
At full power the ATP store in the muscle lasts only about two to three seconds.
The rule of thumb 220 minus age is only a rough estimate and can be wrong by more than ten beats.

teile.einleitung: The football rules set out how a football match is played and what is allowed. They are the same all over the world and are decided by the International Football Association Board, IFAB for short. There are 17 laws, from the size of the pitch to offside.
wichtigste: Each team has eleven players on the pitch at the same time.
A regular adult match lasts 90 minutes without added time.
A penalty is taken from 11 metres away.
After a second yellow card a player is shown a red card and sent off.
A goal only counts if the ball has completely crossed the goal line.
There is no offside from a throw-in.
VAR stands for video assistant referee.

abschnitte.text: For international matches the pitch is between 100 and 110 metres long and 64 to 75 metres wide. A match lasts two times 45 minutes, plus **added time** (stoppage time) for interruptions. In knockout matches there can be extra time of two times 15 minutes and a penalty shootout. In most competitions each team may make five substitutions.

A **goal** only counts if the ball has completely crossed the goal line between the posts and under the crossbar. If only part of the ball is on the line, it does not count. In big leagues **goal-line technology** helps with this, telling the referee immediately via a watch whether the ball was in. The team with more goals wins.

A player is **offside** if, when the ball is played, they are nearer to the opponents' goal line than both the ball and the second-to-last opponent. It is only punished if they actively take part in play. There is no offside in your own half. If a player receives the ball directly from a throw-in, a corner kick or a goal kick, they are not offside either.

For a foul the other team gets a **free kick**, and in the fouling team's own penalty area a penalty from 11 metres. For unsporting behaviour the referee shows the yellow card. Anyone who receives a second yellow card in the same match is shown a **second yellow and a red** and has to leave the pitch. For serious foul play there is a straight red card, and the team then plays with one player fewer.

For a **throw-in** you have to throw the ball with both hands from behind and over your head, keeping both feet on the ground. Since the 2018 World Cup the **VAR**, the video assistant referee, has been used at big tournaments. It checks goals, penalties, red cards and cases of mistaken identity on a screen. If things are unclear, the referee can watch the scene at the side of the pitch themselves.

begriffe.erklaerung: The body that sets the football rules that apply worldwide.
A rule against attackers waiting behind the defence.
Extra minutes at the end of a half to make up for interruptions.
An undisturbed kick for the team that was fouled.
Video assistant referee, who checks disputed situations.

gewusst: Yellow and red cards were only introduced at the 1970 World Cup in Mexico.
IFAB was founded as early as 1886 and consists of the four British associations and FIFA.
The goalkeeper may not pick up a back pass played with the foot; this rule has existed since 1992.

teile.einleitung: Albert Einstein was one of the most famous physicists of all time. His theory of relativity changed our understanding of space, time and gravity. He developed many of his most important ideas in Switzerland, when he was working at the patent office in Bern.
wichtigste: Albert Einstein was born in Ulm in Germany in 1879 and died in the USA in 1955.
He took his school-leaving exam in Aarau and studied in Zurich at the Polytechnic, today’s ETH.
In 1901 he became a Swiss citizen.
While at the patent office in Bern, he published the special theory of relativity in 1905.
The formula E = mc² shows that mass and energy are connected.
In 1915 he presented the general theory of relativity.
In 1921 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

abschnitte.text: Einstein grew up in Munich and did not like the strict lessons at school. At 16 he came to Switzerland and in 1896 passed the **Matura, the school-leaving exam, at the cantonal school in Aarau**. He then studied physics and mathematics at the Polytechnic in Zurich, today’s **ETH Zurich**. In 1901 he became a Swiss citizen and remained one all his life. At first he could not find a job at a university after his studies.

From 1902 Einstein worked as an expert at the **patent office in Bern**, checking inventions. In his free time he thought about physics. In 1905 he published several groundbreaking papers at once, which is why it is called his **miracle year**. In them he explained, among other things, the photoelectric effect, the movement of tiny particles in liquids and the **special theory of relativity**. His flat at Kramgasse 49 is now the Einstein House, a museum.

The special theory of relativity says that time and space are not the same for everyone. If you move very fast, time passes more slowly. From this follows the famous formula **E = mc²**: mass can be turned into energy. In 1915 in Berlin he presented the **general theory of relativity**, which explains gravity as a curving of space and time. However, he received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921 for explaining the photoelectric effect.

From 1914 Einstein lived in Berlin and became world famous. Because he was Jewish, he left Germany in 1933 when the National Socialists came to power. He moved to **Princeton** in the USA and did research there until his death in 1955. In 1939 he warned President Roosevelt in a letter that Germany might build an atomic bomb. Later he campaigned strongly for peace and against nuclear weapons.

Without Einstein’s theories, for example, the **GPS** in mobile phones would not be accurate. His ideas help us understand black holes and the Big Bang. Today Einstein is seen as a symbol of a genius. The photo of him sticking his tongue out is known all over the world. The element einsteinium was named after him.

begriffe.erklaerung: Einstein’s theory about space, time and gravity.
An authority that checks and protects inventions.
A formula that shows that mass and energy are connected.
Light can knock electrons out of a metal.

gewusst: Einstein did not fail maths, as is often claimed; he was very good at it.
At the patent office in Bern he was employed as a “technical expert, third class”.
In 1952 Einstein was offered the post of President of Israel, but he turned it down.

teile.einleitung: First aid means helping immediately after an accident or in an emergency until the ambulance service arrives. Something can quickly happen during sport too. If you know the most important steps and emergency numbers, you can save lives.
wichtigste: In Switzerland you reach the ambulance on 144 and Rega on 1414.
The police number is 117, the fire brigade 118.
Never put ice directly on the skin; always put a cloth in between.
Unconscious people who are breathing normally are put into the recovery position.
For resuscitation of adults the rule is 30 compressions to 2 rescue breaths.
If a back injury is suspected, you do not move the person.

abschnitte.text: **144** calls the ambulance, that is the emergency medical service. **117** is the police and **118** the fire brigade. You reach **Rega** (the Swiss air rescue) on **1414**, for example after accidents in the mountains. When you call, say calmly who is calling, what has happened and where. Then stay on the phone until all the questions have been answered.

**Cooling** helps with bruises and sprains. But never put ice directly on the skin, otherwise it can cause **cold injuries**. That is why a cloth belongs in between. You also raise the injured part of the body. For a **nosebleed** after being hit by a ball, lean your head forwards and pinch the soft part of the nose together, so that the blood does not run into your throat.

If someone is **unconscious**, you first check their breathing. If the person is breathing normally, you put them into the **recovery position**. This keeps the airway clear, and any vomit can drain out. You must keep checking their breathing regularly. If a **spinal injury** is suspected, you do not move a person who can respond; you calm them down and wait for the ambulance service.

If a person is not breathing normally, you start **cardiopulmonary resuscitation** (CPR) immediately. With adults, **30 chest compressions** are followed by **2 rescue breaths** each time. You press the breastbone down about **5 to 6 cm**, at 100 to 120 compressions per minute. After each compression the chest must rise back up fully. A **defibrillator** (AED), found at many railway stations and sports grounds, also helps.

gewusst: From abroad you can reach Rega on the number +41 333 333 333.
Anyone in Switzerland who wants to get a driving licence must first attend a first-aid course.

teile.einleitung: Supercompensation is a model from training theory. It explains why training makes you stronger: after an effort the body does not just recover but for a short time builds up beyond its previous level.
wichtigste: The phases are effort, fatigue, recovery and supercompensation.
How long recovery takes depends on the type, intensity and volume of the effort.
If the next effort comes too early, performance drops.
If the break is too long, performance falls back to its starting level.
The model is associated above all with the Soviet researcher Nikolai Yakovlev.
Today it is regarded as a simplification, because the body's systems recover at different speeds.

abschnitte.text: First comes the **effort**, for example a run or a strength session. This is followed by **fatigue**: performance is lower than before. During **recovery** the body rebuilds its reserves. In the phase of **supercompensation** performance is above its starting level for a short time.

According to the model, the next training stimulus should come in the time window of supercompensation. If you always train again during the fatigue phase, the fatigue adds up and performance **decreases**. In the long run there is a risk of **overtraining**. If, on the other hand, the break is far too long, performance returns to the old level. How long recovery takes depends on the **type, intensity and volume** of the effort, but also on age, sleep and diet.

The classic model is associated above all with the Soviet sports biochemist **Nikolai Yakovlev**. He studied how the store of **muscle glycogen** refills after exercise. Glycogen is a storage form of carbohydrates. After being emptied and then recovering, the store was larger than before. **Carb-loading** before endurance competitions also uses this principle.

Today the model is regarded as a **simplification**. Energy stores, muscles, tendons and the nervous system recover **at different speeds**, and a single curve cannot show this exactly. Nevertheless the idea helps with planning. Before important competitions athletes use **tapering**: they reduce the volume of training but largely keep the intensity, so that they are fresh on competition day.

gewusst: The term supercompensation literally means “over-balancing”.
Training does not make you stronger during the effort but only during the recovery afterwards.

teile.einleitung: “Avatar” is a science fiction film from 2009 by the Canadian director James Cameron. It is set on the distant moon Pandora, where blue-skinned beings live in harmony with nature. With its spectacular 3D images it became the most successful film of all time, measured by worldwide takings without adjusting for inflation (as of 2026).
wichtigste: Avatar came out in cinemas in December 2009.
It was directed by James Cameron, who also made “Titanic”.
The film is set on Pandora, a moon with lush jungle.
The native people are called the Na’vi; they are about three metres tall and blue.
The film took about 2.9 billion US dollars worldwide.
It won three Oscars, including one for visual effects.
There are sequels; “The Way of Water” came out in 2022.

abschnitte.text: In the year 2154, humans are mining a valuable raw material on **Pandora**. The paralysed former soldier **Jake Sully** controls an artificial Na’vi body there, a so-called avatar. He is supposed to win the trust of the native people. But he falls in love with the Na’vi Neytiri and in the end takes the side of the Na’vi.

Pandora is a moon that circles a giant gas planet. There are floating mountains, glowing plants and strange animals. The **Na’vi** live in a gigantic tree and are connected to animals and nature through their braids of hair. In this way the film shows how important it is to protect **nature**.

For Avatar the technique of **motion capture** was developed much further. The actors wore suits with markers, and cameras transferred their movements and facial expressions onto the computer characters. James Cameron had his own **3D cameras** built for the film. Many cinemas switched to 3D projection because of it.

Avatar took about 2.9 billion US dollars worldwide, making it the most successful film without adjusting for inflation (as of 2026). For a time “Avengers: Endgame” overtook it, but after a re-release in China in 2021 Avatar was back in front. The film won three **Oscars**: for cinematography, production design and visual effects. The main roles were played by Sam Worthington and **Zoe Saldaña**.

In December 2022 “Avatar: The Way of Water” came out, which is set mainly under water. This film is also one of the most successful of all time. At the end of 2025 the third part, “Avatar: Fire and Ash”, followed. More **sequels** are planned.

begriffe.erklaerung: In the film, an artificial body that a human controls with their mind.
A technique that transfers the movements of real people onto computer characters.
The money a film earns from cinema tickets sold.
When prices rise over time and money becomes worth less.

gewusst: A language of its own with more than a thousand words was invented for the Na’vi.
James Cameron had the idea back in the 1990s but waited for better technology.

teile.einleitung: A film adaptation is a film based on a book, a play or another literary source. Many of the most famous films, from “Harry Potter” to “Heidi”, are adaptations like this. A story made of words has to be translated into pictures, sounds and scenes.
wichtigste: A film adaptation turns a book or a play into a film.
The “Harry Potter” films are based on the books by J. K. Rowling.
The “Heidi” books by the Swiss writer Johanna Spyri have been filmed many times.
The “Lord of the Rings” films were shot mainly in New Zealand.
The books by the Swedish writer Astrid Lindgren have often been filmed.
Michael Ende's “The Neverending Story” came to the cinema in 1984.
In 1967 Disney made Rudyard Kipling's “The Jungle Book” into a cartoon.

abschnitte.text: In a **film adaptation** a book, a story or a play serves as the **source**. Because a film lasts only about two hours, characters, scenes or whole subplots often have to be left out. Thoughts and feelings described in the book have to be shown in the film through pictures, music and acting. From this a screenplay is written, the so-called **adaptation**. Some adaptations stay close to the book, others change the story a great deal.

abschnitte.titel: Harry Potter and The Lord of the Rings
abschnitte.text: The seven books about **Harry Potter** by J. K. Rowling were made into eight films from 2001 to 2011. The films made the young actors such as Daniel Radcliffe world-famous. **J. R. R. Tolkien's** “The Lord of the Rings” was filmed by Peter Jackson, and the three films came out from 2001 to 2003. They were shot mainly in **New Zealand**, whose landscapes represented Middle-earth. The third part won eleven Oscars.

The “**Heidi**” books by the Swiss writer Johanna Spyri are among the most frequently filmed books of all. There are Heidi films from Switzerland, the USA and Germany, as well as a well-known Japanese cartoon series from the 1970s. In 2015 a new Swiss Heidi film came to the cinema with Bruno Ganz as the grandfather (the Alpöhi). In the same year **Ursli** (Schellen-Ursli) from the Engadine, who looks for a big bell for Chalandamarz, was also filmed. Both films show the Swiss mountains.

The books by the Swedish writer **Astrid Lindgren**, for example about Pippi Longstocking or Emil of Lönneberga, were often filmed in Sweden. Michael Ende's “**The Neverending Story**” came to the cinema in 1984. In Erich Kästner's book “Lottie and Lisa” (Das doppelte Lottchen) the **twin sisters** Luise and Lotte discover at a holiday camp that they have grown up apart. In “The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe” by C. S. Lewis children reach a magic land through a **wardrobe**. Roald Dahl's “Charlie and the Chocolate Factory” with the factory owner Willy Wonka was filmed in 1971 and 2005.

**Walt Disney** made many books and fairy tales into cartoons, such as “Snow White”, “Pinocchio” or “Peter Pan”. In 1967 “**The Jungle Book**” came out, based on the stories by Rudyard Kipling. In it the boy Mowgli grows up among wolves and is protected by Baloo the bear and Bagheera the panther. Disney often changed the source material a lot, made it funnier and added songs. Later, remakes with real actors were made of many of these films.

Many people argue about whether the book or the film is better. A book leaves more room for the **imagination**, because you picture the characters and places yourself. A film, on the other hand, can impress with pictures, music and special effects. People often read the book after seeing a film, or the other way round. Comparing a book and its film is a popular task in lessons.

begriffe.erklaerung: The book or play on which a film is based.
Reworking a book for a different form, for example for a film.
A new film version of a story that has already been filmed.
A novel on which a film is based.

gewusst: Michael Ende was so unhappy with the film of “The Neverending Story” that he wanted his name removed from the opening credits.
In New Zealand you can visit the film set of the hobbit village of Hobbiton today.
Heidi also exists as a Japanese cartoon series that was shown in many countries.

teile.einleitung: The Benz Patent Motor Car Number 1 is considered the world’s first practical motor car. Carl Benz applied for a patent for it in Germany on 29 January 1886. The vehicle had three wheels and a small petrol engine, and it went about as fast as a bicycle.
wichtigste: Carl Benz applied for a patent for the motor car in 1886.
It is considered the first car with a petrol engine.
The vehicle had three wheels and looked like a carriage without a horse.
The engine had less than 1 horsepower.
Its top speed was about 16 km/h.
In 1888 Bertha Benz made the first long car journey in history.
Carl Benz’s company later became Mercedes-Benz.

abschnitte.text: The **Patent Motor Car** was a light tricycle with a steel tube frame and spoked wheels. At the front it had a single wheel that could be steered with a crank. At the back sat a horizontal **single-cylinder four-stroke engine** with a capacity of just under 1 litre. It produced about 0.75 horsepower, so less than one horse.

**Carl Benz** was born near Karlsruhe in 1844 and was an engineer. In his workshop in **Mannheim** he built engines and finally a whole vehicle around one. On 29 January 1886 he applied for the patent with the number 37435. At about the same time Gottlieb Daimler and Wilhelm Maybach were also developing a motor car in Stuttgart.

In 1888 **Bertha Benz**, Carl’s wife, drove with her two sons from Mannheim to **Pforzheim**. The route was about 100 kilometres long. She bought the petrol on the way at a **chemist’s** in Wiesloch, because there were no filling stations yet. With this journey she proved that the car was fit for everyday use.

The engine burnt petrol and in this way moved a piston up and down. The power was passed to the rear wheels through a large **flywheel** and belts. The engine was cooled with water, which evaporated in the process. An **ignition** with an electric spark lit the mixture of petrol and air.

The motor car is seen as the **birth of the automobile**. The original is now in the Deutsches Museum in Munich, and there are replicas in many museums. The companies of Benz and Daimler became the **Mercedes-Benz** brand in 1926. Today well over a billion cars are on the road worldwide.

begriffe.erklaerung: A protective right that guarantees an inventor sole use of an invention for a time.
An engine that takes in, compresses, ignites and pushes out in four steps.
An old unit for the power of an engine (German PS).
The space in which the piston moves inside the engine.

gewusst: Because Bertha Benz bought petrol at a chemist’s on the way, the one in Wiesloch is considered the world’s first filling station.
Going uphill, Bertha and her sons sometimes had to push the car.

teile.einleitung: When you do sport, you sweat and lose water. That is why drinking is very important during sport. The best thing to drink is water, regularly and in small sips.
wichtigste: Water is the best drink during sport.
The body loses water through sweating.
You drink before you get very thirsty.
Sweat cools the body.
It is best to drink in small sips.
When it is hot, you need to drink more.
Your own water bottle belongs at every sports event.

abschnitte.text: During sport the muscles work and the body gets warm. So that it does not **overheat**, you sweat. The **sweat** evaporates on the skin, and this makes the skin cooler. In this way sweat helps to **cool** the body. But water is lost with the sweat, and you have to give it back to the body.

**Water** quenches your thirst and contains no sugar. That is why it is the best drink for children during sport. Sugary drinks often contain a lot of sugar. In Switzerland you can often fill up with water straight from a **fountain** if there is no sign saying “Kein Trinkwasser” (not drinking water). Tap water from the mains is also good drinking water in Switzerland.

When you are very thirsty, your body is already short of water. That is why you drink **regularly**, before you get very thirsty. It is best to take **small sips**, which is more comfortable for your stomach. A little more often is better than a lot rarely. Drinking before and after sport is important too.

abschnitte.titel: In the heat and on the move
abschnitte.text: When it is **hot**, you sweat more and therefore need to drink more. For a sports day, a training session or a **hike**, it is best to take your own **water bottle**. That way you can drink at any time. Together with a cap and sun cream, you are well equipped on hot days.

gewusst: More than half of a child's body is made of water.
If you drink too little, you can get tired and have a headache.

teile.einleitung: A world record is the best performance ever officially measured in an event. In sport, world records are checked and recognised by the international federations. Some records last only a few months, others have stood for decades.
wichtigste: In 2009 Usain Bolt ran the 100 metres in Berlin in 9.58 seconds (as of 2026).
In 1988 Florence Griffith-Joyner ran the women's 100 metres in 10.49 seconds.
In 1991 Mike Powell jumped 8.95 metres.
Javier Sotomayor holds the high jump world record of 2.45 metres.
Since 2020 Armand Duplantis has kept improving the pole vault world record.
Michael Phelps won a total of 28 Olympic medals.
In April 2026 in London, Sabastian Sawe became the first person to run an official marathon in under two hours.

abschnitte.text: In 2009 **Usain Bolt** from Jamaica ran the 100 metres in **9.58 seconds** at the World Championships in Berlin. That is an average of over 37 kilometres per hour. For women, **Florence Griffith-Joyner** from the USA has held the record of 10.49 seconds since 1988. As of 2026 neither record has been broken.

In 1991 in Tokyo the American **Mike Powell** jumped 8.95 metres, which is still the world record today. In the high jump the Cuban **Javier Sotomayor** has held the record of 2.45 metres since 1993. Since 2020 the Swede **Armand Duplantis** has kept improving the pole vault world record. He usually raises it by just one centimetre, and by the mid-2020s it was already well over 6.20 metres.

The American **Michael Phelps** is the most successful Olympian in history. He won a total of 28 Olympic medals, 23 of them gold. In Beijing in 2008 he won eight gold medals at a single Games, which is also a record. Along the way he set many world records.

abschnitte.titel: A marathon in under two hours
abschnitte.text: For a long time a marathon in under two hours was considered almost impossible. In 2019 Eliud Kipchoge managed it in Vienna, but in a special run that does not count as an official record. In April 2026 in London **Sabastian Sawe** became the first person to run under two hours in an official marathon. A marathon is 42.195 kilometres long.

For a **world record** to count, it must be measured under exact conditions. In athletics, for example, the federation World Athletics checks the **wind measurement** and the timing. If there is too much tailwind, a sprint or jump record does not count. A doping test is part of it too. Besides sporting records, the Guinness Book of Records also contains many funny best performances.

begriffe.erklaerung: The best officially recognised performance in the world in an event.
Wind from behind, which helps when running and jumping.
The world federation for athletics.
A long-distance race over 42.195 kilometres.

gewusst: During his record run Usain Bolt briefly reached over 44 kilometres per hour.
Mike Powell's long jump world record is older than most of the athletes competing today.
With a tailwind of more than 2 metres per second a sprint record is not recognised.

teile.einleitung: The Olympic Movement includes the International Olympic Committee, the sports federations and the Olympic Games. Switzerland plays a special role in it, because the IOC has its headquarters in Lausanne. The Paralympic Games are also an important part of world sport.
wichtigste: Since 1915 the IOC has had its headquarters in Lausanne.
The Olympic Museum in Lausanne opened in 1993.
In 2020 Lausanne hosted the Winter Youth Olympic Games.
The Olympic rings stand for the union of the five continents.
The first Paralympics took place in Rome in 1960, founded by Ludwig Guttmann.
Since 1994 the Summer and Winter Games have alternated every two years.

abschnitte.text: The **International Olympic Committee** (IOC) was founded in Paris in 1894. The driving force was the Frenchman **Pierre de Coubertin**. During the First World War he moved its headquarters to neutral **Lausanne** in **1915**. Since then Lausanne has been regarded as the Olympic Capital. According to the **Olympic Charter**, the IOC may have at most **115** regular members.

The five **Olympic rings** are linked together. According to Coubertin's idea, they stand for the union of the **five continents** through sport. Their colours together with the white background were meant to be able to show the flags of all nations. The **Olympic Charter** contains the rules of the movement. It is written in French and English, and if there are contradictions the **French** version applies.

The **Olympic Museum** on the shore of Lake Geneva opened in **1993**. It shows the history and the present of the Games. In January **2020** the third **Winter Youth Olympic Games** took place in **Lausanne**. Some competitions were also held in other places such as St Moritz. St Moritz had already hosted the Olympic Winter Games in 1928 and 1948.

The doctor **Ludwig Guttmann** is regarded as the founder of the **Paralympic Movement**. In **1948** he organised competitions for war-injured wheelchair users at Stoke Mandeville in England. These developed into the **Paralympic Games**. The first ones took place in **Rome in 1960**, following the Summer Games. About 400 athletes took part.

In the past the Summer and Winter Games took place in the same year. In **1994** in **Lillehammer** the Winter Games were held two years after the Summer Games for the first time. Since then there have been Olympic Games every two years, alternating between summer and winter. That way both get more attention. But each kind still takes place every four years.

gewusst: Besides the IOC, many international sports federations also have their headquarters in Switzerland, especially in the Lausanne region.
Pierre de Coubertin is buried in Lausanne, but his heart lies in Olympia in Greece.

teile.einleitung: The banana is one of the most popular fruits in the world and grows in warm, tropical countries. Although it is long and curved, in botany it counts as a berry. The plant it grows on looks like a tree but is actually a giant herbaceous plant.
wichtigste: Botanically speaking, the banana is a berry.
The banana plant is not a tree but a giant herbaceous plant.
Bananas originally come from South East Asia.
They grow in bunches made up of “hands”.
Bananas contain a lot of potassium and carbohydrates.
Most bananas in the shops belong to the Cavendish variety.
Switzerland imports its bananas, mostly from Central and South America.

abschnitte.text: The banana plant grows several metres tall and has huge leaves. Its **false stem** is not made of wood but of leaf sheaths tightly rolled on top of each other. On a long fruit stalk, many bananas grow in groups called **hands**. A single banana is also called a finger.

In botany a **berry** is a fruit that grows from a single ovary and has soft flesh. That is exactly true of the banana. Wild bananas have many hard seeds inside. In the bananas we eat, only tiny black dots are left of them.

Bananas come from **South East Asia** and were grown there thousands of years ago. Today they grow in many tropical countries, for example Ecuador, Costa Rica, Colombia, India and the Philippines. **Ecuador** is one of the biggest exporters in the world. After the harvest, the part of the plant above ground dies, and a new plant grows from the rootstock.

Bananas are harvested green and taken to Europe in refrigerated ships. In so-called **ripening rooms** they are made to turn yellow with the plant gas **ethylene**. Only then do they go into the shops. In Switzerland the Fairtrade organisation Max Havelaar has made sure that many bananas come from fair trade.

Bananas provide energy quickly and are therefore popular with athletes. They contain a lot of **potassium**, which is important for muscles and nerves. Their skin protects them well and makes them easy to take with you. As well as sweet dessert bananas, there are also **plantains**, which are fried or cooked.

begriffe.erklaerung: A fruit with soft flesh that grows from a single ovary.
A plant without a woody stem.
A gas that makes fruit ripen.
Trade in which the farmers receive a fair price.

gewusst: As they grow, bananas bend upwards, towards the light.
Most bananas worldwide are clones, that is genetically almost identical, which is why they are vulnerable to diseases.

teile.einleitung: There are often a great many people on the ski slopes at the same time. To prevent accidents, the International Ski Federation FIS has drawn up ten rules of conduct. They apply to skiers, snowboarders and everyone else on the slopes.
wichtigste: You ski in such a way that you can stop or swerve at any time.
Before joining a slope or setting off, you look uphill.
When overtaking, you leave enough space.
You do not stop in narrow places or places where others cannot see you.
On foot you walk at the edge of the slope.
If there is an accident, you must help and give your name and address.

abschnitte.text: The most important rule is **consideration**: nobody should endanger others. You adapt your **speed** to your own ability, the terrain and the snow. You should be able to **stop at any time** or swerve. Anyone coming from behind must ski in such a way that they do not endanger the people in front. The skiers and riders further down have priority.

You may **overtake** on the left or the right, but always with **enough space**. The person being overtaken needs room for their movements. Before you join a slope or set off again after stopping, you **look uphill** and downhill. That way you do not collide with others. You also look carefully when moving uphill or crossing the slope.

You do not stop in **narrow** places or places where you **cannot be seen** clearly, because others will have trouble seeing you there. It is better to stop at the edge in a clearly visible spot. Anyone who falls clears the spot as quickly as possible. Anyone **on foot** uses the **edge** of the slope. You also pay attention to the **markings and signs**, which warn, for example, of dangers or closed slopes.

If there is an accident, everyone is obliged to **help**. You can, for example, mark the accident site with crossed skis above it and fetch help. In Switzerland you alert the piste rescue service, the ambulance on 144 or Rega on 1414. The last rule is the **duty to identify yourself**. Everyone involved and all witnesses give their **name and address**.

gewusst: The FIS rules have existed since 1967 and have been revised several times since then.
The rules are also used as a standard in court when it has to be decided who is to blame after a skiing accident.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland has been a full member of the United Nations, the UN for short, since 10 September 2002. Before that it had hesitated for a long time, because many people feared losing the country’s neutrality. Only in a popular vote in March 2002 did the voters narrowly say yes to joining.
wichtigste: Switzerland joined the UN as a full member in 2002.
The popular vote took place on 3 March 2002.
About 55 per cent of voters said yes.
The majority of the cantons was very narrow.
In 1986 the people had still clearly rejected joining.
Switzerland became the 190th member of the UN.
Geneva has long been one of the most important UN locations.

abschnitte.text: The **United Nations** was founded in 1945 after the Second World War. Its aims are to keep the peace, protect human rights and encourage countries to work together. Its headquarters are in **New York**. Today almost all the countries in the world are members, namely 193 (as of 2026).

In 1986 the Swiss voted on joining, and about three quarters said no. Many were afraid that **neutrality** could suffer. A **popular initiative** brought the issue before the people again. On 3 March 2002 about 55 per cent then said yes, and the majority of the cantons narrowly agreed as well.

On **10 September 2002** Switzerland was admitted at the General Assembly in New York. It was the 190th member. Shortly afterwards East Timor joined as the 191st member. Switzerland was one of the few countries to join the UN through a **popular vote**.

Long before joining, Switzerland was closely linked to the UN. In **Geneva** stands the Palais des Nations, the UN’s European headquarters. Organisations such as the World Health Organization WHO and the UN Refugee Agency also work there. Even before 2002 Switzerland took part in many UN organisations, but it had no vote in the **General Assembly**.

As a member, Switzerland can have its say and vote in the UN. In 2023 and 2024 it was a non-permanent member of the **Security Council** for the first time. In the UN, Switzerland works especially for humanitarian aid, human rights and peacebuilding. It has kept its neutrality while doing so.

begriffe.erklaerung: The United Nations, an organisation of almost all the countries in the world.
A country does not take sides in wars between other countries.
The most important UN body for peace and security, with 15 members.
The majority of the cantons in a popular vote (German “Ständemehr”).

gewusst: Switzerland is one of very few countries in which the people were allowed to vote on joining the UN.
The Palais des Nations in Geneva used to be the seat of the League of Nations, the forerunner of the UN.

teile.einleitung: Volleyball is a net game in which two teams play a ball over a high net. The ball must not touch the ground in your own court. It is played indoors or as beach volleyball on sand.
wichtigste: In indoor volleyball each team has six players on the court.
A set goes up to 25 points, with a lead of at least 2 points.
The deciding set goes up to 15 points.
The libero is the defensive specialist with a different-coloured shirt.
In a dig (forearm pass) you play the ball with both forearms.
The net is 2.43 m high for men and 2.24 m high for women.
In beach volleyball there are two players per team.

abschnitte.text: Each team may touch the ball **at most three times** before it has to go over the net. If the ball lands on the ground in the opponents' court, you win a point. A set goes up to **25 points**, but you need a lead of at least **2 points**. Whoever wins three sets wins the match. A **deciding set** only goes up to 15.

In **indoor volleyball** each team has **six** players on the court, three at the front by the net and three at the back. Each time they win the right to serve, they move on one position; this is called **rotation**. The **libero** is a defensive specialist. They play only at the back, may not attack or block and wear a shirt of a different colour.

In the **dig** or forearm pass you put your forearms together and let the ball bounce off them. This is how you take low and hard balls. In the **volley** (overhead pass) you play the ball with the fingers of both hands above your forehead, usually to set it up for a team-mate. With the **spike** you attack, and with the **block** at the net you defend against attacks.

The top of the net is at **2.43 metres** for men and **2.24 metres** for women. For children and teenagers the net is lower. The court is 18 metres long and 9 metres wide. A line divides each half into a front zone and a back zone.

**Beach volleyball** is played on sand with only **two players** per team. That is why each player must master all the techniques. In Switzerland, for example, the tournament in **Gstaad** is well known. Volleyball was invented in the USA in **1895** by William G. Morgan. Indoor volleyball has been an Olympic sport since 1964, beach volleyball since 1996.

gewusst: Volleyball was originally invented as a less tiring game than basketball.
In beach volleyball partners give each other secret signals with hand signs behind their backs.

teile.einleitung: Alan Turing was a British mathematician and one of the fathers of computer science. During the Second World War he played a major part at Bletchley Park in breaking the secret radio messages of the German Enigma machine. His ideas are still the basis of computers and artificial intelligence today.
wichtigste: Alan Turing lived in England from 1912 to 1954.
In 1936 he described the Turing machine, a model for every computer.
At Bletchley Park he helped to crack the Enigma code.
For this he helped to develop a machine called the Bombe.
With the Turing test he asked whether machines can think.
Because he was homosexual, he was convicted in 1952.
The most important award in computer science is called the Turing Award.

abschnitte.text: Alan Turing was born in London on 23 June 1912. Even as a child he was interested in numbers and the natural sciences. He studied mathematics at the University of **Cambridge**. Later he also did research in the USA at Princeton University. Turing was a keen long-distance runner and ran almost as fast as Olympic athletes.

In 1936 Turing published a famous paper on the limits of mathematics. In it he imagined a simple machine that existed only in thought, the **Turing machine**. It reads and writes symbols on an endless tape and follows fixed rules as it does so. Turing showed that such a machine can carry out any calculation that can be calculated at all. In this way he laid the foundation of **computer science** before real computers even existed.

In the **Second World War** the German armed forces encrypted their radio messages with the **Enigma** machine. Turing worked at **Bletchley Park**, a secret site north of London. Building on the work of Polish mathematicians, he helped to develop the electromechanical machine called the “Bombe”. With it the British were able to read many German messages, including those of the U-boats. Historians believe that this shortened the war and saved many lives.

After the war Turing worked on early computers in London and Manchester. In 1950 he proposed a test that is now called the **Turing test**. A person has a written conversation with an unknown partner. If they cannot tell whether they are writing to a human or a machine, the machine counts as intelligent. With modern chatbots this idea is being widely discussed again.

At that time homosexuality was illegal in Great Britain. Turing was convicted in 1952 and had to undergo hormone treatment. In 1954 he died of cyanide poisoning at only 41. Not until 2013 was he **pardoned** by the British Queen. Since 2021 his picture has been on the British 50-pound note, and the film “The Imitation Game” tells his story.

begriffe.erklaerung: An imagined model of a computer that can carry out any calculation.
German encryption machine from the Second World War.
Changing messages so that only those in the know can read them.
A test of whether a machine behaves like a thinking human.

gewusst: Turing’s work at Bletchley Park was kept top secret for decades.
The Turing Award is seen as the “Nobel Prize of computer science” and has been awarded since 1966.
Turing used the word machine at a time when computers were still people who did calculations by hand.

teile.einleitung: A film studio is a company that makes films, or a large site with halls in which films are shot. Famous studios such as Disney, Pixar or Ghibli have invented characters that children all over the world know. Many of the big studios are in Hollywood near Los Angeles.
wichtigste: A film studio is a film company or a site with halls for shooting.
Walt Disney founded the studio that brought out Mickey Mouse.
Pixar produced films including “Ratatouille” and “Up”.
The animation studio Ghibli is based in Japan.
Aardman from Great Britain invented “Shaun the Sheep”.
In MGM's opening titles a lion roars.
In 2012 Disney bought Lucasfilm and with it the rights to “Star Wars”.
The big film industry in Mumbai is called Bollywood.

abschnitte.text: The word **film studio** has two meanings. It can be a company that plans, pays for and makes films. But it can also be a site with large halls, the **sound stages** or studio halls, in which sets are built. There you can film regardless of the weather and the time of day. Big studios also have their own departments for effects, sound and advertising.

From the 1910s many film studios were set up in the **Hollywood** district of Los Angeles because it is almost always sunny there. The best known include Warner Bros., Paramount, Universal and **Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer**, MGM for short. In MGM's opening titles a lion has been roaring for almost a hundred years. For decades these big studios shaped cinema all over the world. Today the name Hollywood stands for the whole American film industry.

**Walt Disney** founded a cartoon studio with his brother Roy in 1923, and Mickey Mouse appeared in 1928. Today Disney is one of the largest entertainment groups in the world. **Pixar** became famous for computer animation: in 1995 “Toy Story” came out as the first cinema film created entirely on the computer. Later came films such as “Ratatouille” and “Up”, and in 2006 Disney bought the studio. In 2012 Disney also took over **Lucasfilm** and with it the rights to “Star Wars”.

In 2001 **DreamWorks Animation** brought out “Shrek”, the first film to win the Oscar for best animated feature. The studio **Illumination** invented the yellow Minions for the film “Despicable Me”. In Japan Hayao Miyazaki and colleagues founded **Studio Ghibli**, known for “My Neighbour Totoro” and “Spirited Away”. The British studio **Aardman** from Bristol shapes its characters from modelling clay. “Wallace and Gromit” and “Shaun the Sheep” come from there.

The **Babelsberg** studio near Potsdam was founded in 1912 and is regarded as one of the oldest large studios in the world. The silent film “Metropolis” was made there in 1927. The famous **Cinecittà** studio is in Rome. In India a great many films with music and dance are made in Mumbai every year; this film industry is called **Bollywood**. The name combines Bombay, the old name for Mumbai, with Hollywood.

Switzerland has no huge studios like those in Hollywood. The Zurich company **Praesens-Film** was founded in 1924 and produced many classic Swiss films, including “Heidi” from 1952. Today numerous smaller **production companies** make feature films, documentaries and series. Many films are shot in real places in the towns and mountains. International productions also come to Switzerland because of the landscape, for example James Bond films to the Schilthorn.

begriffe.erklaerung: A film company or a site with halls in which films are shot.
A large hall in which sets for film scenes are built.
A studio that makes cartoons, clay animation or computer-animated films.
The big film industry in Mumbai in India.
A large business made up of several companies.

gewusst: For one second of clay animation at Aardman, the figures have to be moved a little again and again for many single pictures.
The MGM lion has been nicknamed Leo from the beginning, even though different lions have been filmed over time.
India produces more feature films every year than almost any other country.

teile.einleitung: Media economics is about how newspapers, television channels, cinemas, streaming services and games companies make money. Media are special products, because they sell content and at the same time our attention. If you understand how media are financed, you also better understand what you get to see.
wichtigste: Media companies make money from advertising, subscriptions, sales and fees.
In Switzerland the company Serafe collects the households' radio and television fee.
A film is used in release windows: first in the cinema, then on streaming or disc, later on television.
In product placement companies pay for their products to appear in films.
The first copy of a media product is expensive; further copies cost almost nothing.
Netflix started in 1997 with a DVD rental service by post.
The audience's limited attention is the most important resource of the media.

abschnitte.text: Media companies usually have several sources of income. They sell content directly, for example as a cinema ticket, a newspaper subscription or a game. Then there is **advertising**, which companies pay for so that many people see their advert. That is why people say media sell twice: content to the audience and the audience to the advertisers. Free newspapers and many apps live almost entirely on advertising.

A cinema film is used in several **release windows** one after the other. First it runs in the cinema, then on streaming services or on disc and later on television. In this way the film earns money again in each phase. In the cinema, the cinema and the distributor share the takings: if a cinema sells 240 tickets at 18 francs and half goes to the distributor, the distributor receives 2160 francs. Until 1948 the big Hollywood studios owned production, distribution and cinemas at the same time; this is called **vertical integration**.

In Switzerland households pay a **radio and television fee**, which is collected by the company Serafe (as of 2026). This money mainly finances the SRG, which includes SRF, RTS, RSI and RTR. Some private local radio stations and regional television channels also receive a share. Large private media houses include the TX Group, Ringier and CH Media. Because Switzerland has four national languages, the individual markets are small, which makes media expensive.

Netflix was founded in the USA in 1997 and at first sent DVDs by post. From 2007 the company offered films for **streaming** over the internet. Today many people pay monthly subscriptions to services such as Netflix, Disney+ or Spotify. With the **long tail**, Chris Anderson described how online providers can also make a lot of money from many niche products together. A shop has only a little space, whereas an online catalogue has almost unlimited space.

With media the **first-copy costs** are very high: a film can cost millions, while each further digital copy costs almost nothing. That is why it pays to sell a product to as many people as possible. Because there are so many offers, the audience's time and attention are scarce; this is called the **attention economy**. Apps and platforms therefore try to hold our attention for as long as possible. In **product placement** advertising is built directly into the plot, for example a particular car in an action film.

begriffe.erklaerung: A period in which a film is shown only in a particular way, for example only in the cinema.
The paid placement of a branded product in a film or series.
The high costs of the first copy of a media product.
The idea that our attention is a scarce and valuable good.
Many small niche products together bring in a lot of money.

gewusst: With many free apps you yourself are the product, because the companies sell the advertising space that you get to see.
In 1948 a court in the USA forced the big Hollywood studios to sell their cinemas.
Netflix went on sending DVDs by post to customers in the USA until 2023.

teile.einleitung: The bicycle, in Switzerland usually called a “Velo”, is a popular means of transport and piece of sports equipment. To be safe on the road, a bike needs certain equipment. There are also traffic rules that you have to know.
wichtigste: At the front the bike light shines white, at the back red.
A bike needs two brakes, one at the front and one at the back.
In Switzerland the bike bell is part of the required equipment.
Before turning you show the direction with your arm stretched out.
Since 2021 children under 12 have been allowed to ride on the pavement if there is no cycle path.

abschnitte.text: A bike must have **two brakes**: one for the front wheel and one for the back wheel. It also needs a **bell**, so that you can warn others. **Reflectors** at the front, at the back and on the pedals make the bike visible in the dark. You check the brakes, tyres and lights regularly. A well-adjusted bike is also more comfortable to ride.

At dusk, at night and in tunnels the bike needs **lights**. At the front a **white** or slightly yellow light shines so that people coming towards you can see you. At the back a **red** light shines for the cars behind you. Light-coloured clothing or a high-visibility vest also helps. If you are seen, you are much safer.

Before **turning** you stretch out your arm in the direction you want to go. That way others know what you are about to do. Beforehand you look behind you to see whether a car is coming. You ride on the right-hand edge of the road, but not right next to the kerb. At junctions you pay attention to traffic lights, signs and right of way.

Since **2021** children under **12** have been allowed to ride on the **pavement** if there is no cycle path or cycle lane. They must be considerate towards pedestrians. At school many children take a **cycling test**, where the traffic police explain the rules. A **bike helmet** protects your head if you fall. In Switzerland it is not compulsory for normal bikes, but it is strongly recommended.

gewusst: The first steerable running machine without pedals was built by Karl Drais in 1817.
Switzerland has a large network of signposted cycle routes, called “Veloland Schweiz” (SwitzerlandMobility cycling routes).

teile.einleitung: Swiss Sport Integrity is the independent Swiss body for clean and fair sport. It fights doping and receives reports of ethical violations in sport.
wichtigste: The foundation was set up in 2008 as Antidoping Switzerland.
Since the start of 2022 it has been called Swiss Sport Integrity.
It is based in Bern.
It carries out doping tests in Swiss sport.
Since 2022 it has also been the reporting office for ethical violations in sport.

abschnitte.titel: From Antidoping Switzerland to Swiss Sport Integrity
abschnitte.text: The foundation **Antidoping Switzerland** was set up in **2008**. At the start of **2022** it was given the new name **Swiss Sport Integrity** because it received an additional task: it is now also responsible for ethical violations in sport. Its headquarters are in **Bern**. The International Olympic Committee, on the other hand, has its headquarters in Lausanne.

**Doping** means using banned substances or methods to improve performance. It is unfair and can harm your health. Swiss Sport Integrity carries out **doping tests** in Switzerland, during competitions and also in training. It also works on **prevention**: it informs athletes and coaches about what is allowed and what is not. Suspected cases are investigated.

Since 2022 **ethical violations** in Swiss sport can be reported to Swiss Sport Integrity. These include, for example, **discrimination** or **bullying**. The basis is the **Ethics Statute of Swiss Sport**. The office investigates such reports so that everyone in sport can feel safe and respected.

gewusst: The World Anti-Doping Agency WADA was founded in Lausanne in 1999.

teile.einleitung: The history of sport tells how people held competitions thousands of years ago and how today's sports came about. It is a long way from the ancient Olympic Games in Greece to modern professional sport. Many popular games such as football, basketball and volleyball only appeared in the 19th century.
wichtigste: According to tradition, the first Olympic Games took place in Olympia in 776 BC.
In 1863 the first standard football rules were laid down in England.
The tennis tournament at Wimbledon has existed since 1877.
James Naismith invented basketball in the USA in 1891.
William G. Morgan invented volleyball in 1895.
The first Tour de France took place in 1903.
The world football federation FIFA has its headquarters in Zurich.

abschnitte.text: Wrestling matches and running races already existed in ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia. The most famous competitions of ancient times were the **Olympic Games** at the sanctuary of **Olympia** in Greece. According to tradition, they took place for the first time in 776 BC, in honour of the god Zeus. There were running, wrestling, long jump, discus and javelin throwing and chariot races. Towards the end of the 4th century AD the Games were banned.

In the 19th century many modern sports developed in England. In 1863 the Football Association in London laid down the first standard **football rules**. In 1877 the first tennis tournament took place at Wimbledon. In the USA **James Naismith** invented basketball in 1891 so that his students could play indoors in winter. Four years later, in 1895, William G. Morgan invented volleyball.

The Frenchman **Pierre de Coubertin** wanted to revive the ancient Games. In 1894 the International Olympic Committee was founded in Paris. The first modern Games took place in Athens in 1896. The first Olympic Winter Games were held in Chamonix in 1924. St Moritz hosted the Winter Games in 1928 and 1948.

The first **Tour de France** took place in 1903 and is today the most famous cycle race in the world. The first football World Cup was held in Uruguay in 1930. For a long time women were not allowed to take part in many competitions. Only gradually were their sports added to the programme of the Olympic Games.

In Switzerland a strong **gymnastics movement** developed in the 19th century, and the first Federal Gymnastics Festival took place in Aarau in 1832. The English brought winter sports to the Alps, especially to St Moritz and Davos. Today many sports federations have their headquarters in Switzerland. **FIFA** is in Zurich, the IOC in Lausanne and the European football federation UEFA in Nyon.

begriffe.erklaerung: The time of ancient Greece and Rome, about 2000 to 3000 years ago.
A sanctuary in Greece where the ancient Games took place.
The International Olympic Committee, which organises the Olympic Games.
The world football federation, based in Zurich.

gewusst: At the ancient Olympic Games the athletes competed naked.
The first basketball basket was a peach basket, from which the ball had to be fetched out again after every basket.
The Olympic Museum in Lausanne tells the whole history of the Games.

teile.einleitung: The tennis rules decide how points are counted, when a ball is good and how a match is won. The scoring with 15, 30 and 40 is especially unusual and surprises many beginners. The rules are set by the International Tennis Federation ITF.
wichtigste: Within a game the score goes 15, 30, 40 and then game.
A score of 40 all is called deuce.
Each player has two attempts at serving for each point.
A normal tiebreak goes to 7 points with a lead of 2 points.
If a serve touches the net and lands in the correct box, it is called a let.
There are four Grand Slam tournaments each year.
Wimbledon is played on grass.

abschnitte.text: A match consists of sets, a set of games and a game of points. Within a game the score goes 0, 15, 30, 40 and then game. If the score is 40 all, it is called **deuce**. Then you need two points in a row: the first gives you the **advantage**, the second wins the game. In English, zero is called “love”.

Every point begins with a **serve** from behind the baseline, diagonally into the service box opposite. You have **two attempts** for each point. If both fail, it is a **double fault** and the opponent wins the point. If the ball touches the net on the serve but still lands in the correct box, it is a **let**, and the serve is taken again.

A set is won by whoever first wins six games with a lead of at least two games. If the score is 6 all, a **tiebreak** is usually played. It is won by whoever first reaches 7 points with a lead of 2 points. At the Grand Slam tournaments men play best of five sets, women best of three.

A tennis court is 23.77 metres long and, for singles, 8.23 metres wide. For **doubles** the outer side strips, the tramlines, are added on each side. A ball that touches the line still counts as good. Today an electronic camera system such as **Hawk-Eye** often checks whether a ball was in.

There are four **Grand Slam tournaments** each year: the Australian Open, the French Open, Wimbledon and the US Open. They are played on different surfaces. Wimbledon is on **grass**, Roland Garros in Paris on red clay and the tournaments in Melbourne and New York on hard courts. On clay the ball bounces more slowly and higher, on grass fast and low.

begriffe.erklaerung: The smallest unit of play, made up of several points.
A score of 40 all.
A deciding game at 6 all in a set.
A serve that touches the net, lands in the correct box and is taken again.
Both serving attempts fail, and the opponent wins the point.

gewusst: Where the scoring 15, 30, 40 comes from is not certain; one idea traces it back to the face of a clock.
The longest match in history, at Wimbledon in 2010, lasted over eleven hours, spread over three days.
The net is a little lower in the middle than at the posts.

teile.einleitung: Rhythm is the time pattern of music, that is the sequence of long and short notes and rests. It makes it possible for us to clap, dance or tap our foot to music. But rhythm does not exist only in music: it is also found in speech, in the heartbeat and in walking.
wichtigste: Rhythm is the order of notes and rests in time.
The steady beat you can clap along to is called the pulse.
The speed of a piece of music is called the tempo.
A metronome ticks evenly and helps you practise.
A place where you briefly do not play is called a rest.
Vertical lines divide the music into bars.
In a waltz you always count “one, two, three”.

abschnitte.text: Under almost all music there is a steady beat, the **pulse** or basic beat. That is what you clap to when you join in. The rhythm is what happens on top of it: long and short notes, stresses and rests. You can imagine the pulse like the ticking hand of a clock and the rhythm like a tune made of steps, sometimes fast, sometimes slow.

In written music the shape of a note shows how long it lasts. A **semibreve** (whole note) is as long as two minims or four crotchets, and a crotchet as long as two quavers. So a minim lasts much longer than a quaver. For every note length there is also a matching **rest**, during which you are silent. Rests are just as important as notes, because they give the music room to breathe.

The speed of a piece is called its **tempo**. It is given with Italian words, such as Adagio for slow, Andante for at a walking pace, Allegro for fast and Presto for very fast. More precisely, tempo is measured in beats per minute, bpm for short. A **metronome** ticks evenly at the chosen tempo; Johann Nepomuk Maelzel had it patented in 1815, and Beethoven was one of the first composers to use metronome markings.

Vertical lines, the **barlines**, divide the music into sections of equal length, the bars. In each bar the first beat is usually stressed most strongly. In a waltz you count “one, two, three”, in a march “one, two”. If a beat that is normally weak is stressed, you get a **syncopation**, which is typical of jazz, pop and reggae.

We meet rhythm everywhere: when walking, in the heartbeat, when rowing or skipping. Speech has a rhythm too, which is why you can clap words in syllables, for example “choc-o-late”. In Africa, Latin America and at the Basel carnival, **drums** play a big role. Rappers speak their lyrics to the rhythm of a beat.

begriffe.erklaerung: The steady basic beat of the music.
The speed of a piece of music.
A device that ticks evenly at the tempo you set.
A section of music between two barlines.
Stress on a beat that would normally be unstressed.

gewusst: A calm heartbeat of about 70 beats per minute roughly matches the tempo Andante.
The parrot Snowball became famous because he can dance in time to music.
A mechanical metronome works with a pendulum whose weight you slide to change the tempo.

teile.einleitung: A children's film is a film made especially for children, with stories, characters and themes that suit their age. There are cartoons, clay animation films and films with real actors. Many children's films are based on famous books such as “Heidi” or “Sams”.
wichtigste: Children's films tell stories that children can understand and that are suitable for them.
The label “6+” means that a film is suitable for children aged 6 and over.
In the 2015 film “Heidi” the Swiss actor Bruno Ganz played the grandfather (the Alpöhi).
The clay figure Pingu comes from Switzerland.
Hans de Beer's little polar bear is called Lars.
“My Neighbour Totoro” is a cartoon from Japan.
Wallace and Gromit are made of modelling clay.
The credits at the end of a film name everyone who took part.

abschnitte.text: A **children's film** is aimed at children and tells stories about friendship, courage, family or adventure. The main characters are often children themselves or animals that you can easily identify with. There are **live-action films** with real actors and **animated films** with characters that are drawn, shaped or created on the computer. The work on the film is led by the **director**. At the end the **credits** roll with the names of everyone who took part.

Cinema films carry an **age rating**, for example “6+”. It means that the film is suitable for children aged 6 and over. In Switzerland experts give recommendations on how old children should be for a film and from what age they may see it with an adult. Some scenes can be too exciting or too sad for younger children. Parents can find out beforehand whether a film is suitable.

In the 2015 film “**Heidi**” the young Anuk Steffen played Heidi and the famous Swiss actor **Bruno Ganz** played the grandfather, the Alpöhi. In the same year “A Bell for Ursli” (Schellen-Ursli) by Xavier Koller came to the cinema. The little penguin **Pingu** is also world-famous, a clay figure by the Swiss animator Otmar Gutmann. Pingu speaks a made-up language that children all over the world understand. The television series ran from 1990 and was shown in many countries.

abschnitte.titel: Children's films from around the world
abschnitte.text: “**My Neighbour Totoro**” by Hayao Miyazaki from 1988 comes from Japan; in it two sisters meet a big, fluffy forest creature. In Great Britain Nick Park created the characters **Wallace and Gromit** out of modelling clay. The little polar bear **Lars** from the books by the Dutch author Hans de Beer got his own cartoon films. The American studios Disney and Pixar shape children's cinema worldwide with films such as “Toy Story”. Many children's films are translated into many languages.

Many children's films are based on books. **Vicky the Viking** (Wickie), a clever Viking boy, comes from books by the Swede Runer Jonsson and became known as a cartoon series and, in 2009, as a live-action film. **Sams** by Paul Maar has blue spots on its face that can be used to make wishes. Pippi Longstocking, Heidi and the books by Roald Dahl have also been filmed several times. It is often exciting to compare the book and the film.

In Switzerland there are special offers for children, such as the cinema club **Zauberlaterne** (Magic Lantern), which was founded in Neuchâtel in 1992. There children aged about 6 to 12 see selected films several times a year and learn how cinema works. Film festivals show their own **children's programmes**. Laughing and feeling the excitement together in the cinema is a special experience. Afterwards it is worth talking about the film.

begriffe.erklaerung: A film with real actors instead of drawn characters.
A film with characters that are drawn, shaped or created on the computer.
The list at the end of a film of everyone who took part.
An indication of the age from which a film is suitable.
An animated film with figures made of modelling clay that are moved picture by picture.

gewusst: For one episode of Pingu the clay figures had to be moved a tiny bit many times for every second of film.
Before his role as Heidi's grandfather, Bruno Ganz was also famous for many serious films for adults.
Today the Zauberlaterne also exists in other countries.

teile.einleitung: A film genre is a group of films that are similar in theme, mood or style. Comedy, western, science fiction and animated film are genres of this kind. If you know the genre, you know roughly what to expect at the cinema.
wichtigste: A film genre sorts films by content and mood.
In a comedy you are meant to laugh a lot.
Westerns take place in the Wild West with cowboys.
Science fiction films are about the future and journeys into space.
Documentaries show real people, animals and events.
The first films were silent films without sound.
Animated films are made of pictures drawn by hand or created on the computer.
Many films mix several genres.

abschnitte.text: The word **genre** means kind or type. Films of one genre have similar themes, settings and characters. A western, for example, is almost always set in the Wild West, and a crime film revolves around a crime. Genres help cinemas, streaming services and viewers to classify films. Films often mix several genres, for example as an **action comedy** or a science fiction adventure.

In a **comedy** fun comes first; it lives on witty dialogue, mishaps and mix-ups. Even in the silent film era Charlie Chaplin made audiences laugh. In a **musical** the characters sing and dance, and the songs move the story on. Famous musicals are “The Sound of Music” and “Mamma Mia!”. Many Disney cartoons also have songs and are therefore related to the musical.

**Westerns** show cowboys, sheriffs and settlers in the Wild West of North America in the 19th century. **Adventure films** tell of exciting journeys and treasure hunts, like the Indiana Jones films. In **fantasy films** there is magic, dragons and magical creatures, for example in “The Lord of the Rings” or “Harry Potter”. Films like these take you away to strange worlds. In them heroes often fight against evil.

**Science fiction** is about the future, distant planets, robots and journeys into space, like “Star Wars” or “E.T.”. In a **crime film** a crime is solved, often by police officers or detectives. A **thriller** builds up great suspense, and horror films set out to frighten viewers. These genres are often only suitable for teenagers or adults. The age rating on the poster shows from what age a film may be seen.

A **documentary** shows real people, animals or events, for example nature films about wild animals or reports about inventions. An **animated film** consists of characters that are drawn, shaped from modelling clay or made on the computer. In 1937 Disney's “Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs” was one of the first feature-length cartoons. In 1995 “Toy Story” came out, the first cinema film created entirely on the computer. Today animated films are among the most successful films of all.

The first films had no sound; they are called **silent films**. Dialogue appeared on title cards, and in the cinema a pianist often played music live alongside. From the end of the 1920s **sound films** (talkies) took over. Later came colour film, widescreen pictures and 3D films. With every new technology new possibilities also arose for the different genres.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of films with a similar theme and mood.
A funny film meant to make you laugh.
A film about real people, animals or events.
A film with characters that are drawn, shaped or created on the computer.
A film without recorded sound from the early days of cinema.

gewusst: Many westerns were not filmed in America at all but in Spain and Italy; they are called spaghetti westerns.
In silent film cinemas there were often musicians who accompanied the films live.
The term science fiction means roughly “invented stories about science”.

teile.einleitung: A games console is a computer built especially for playing video games. A home console is usually connected to the television, while a portable console lets you play on the move. The best-known manufacturers are Nintendo, Sony and Microsoft.
wichtigste: The company Nintendo comes from Japan and used to make playing cards.
Sony makes the PlayStation, Microsoft the Xbox.
The Game Boy was a successful console for playing on the move.
With the controller you steer the games in your hand.
With the Wii you control many games with movements.
With the Nintendo Switch you can play on the television and on the move.
In 2025 the Nintendo Switch 2 came out as its successor.

abschnitte.text: A **games console** is a computer designed entirely for games. A **home console** is usually connected to a television. A **handheld console** has its own screen and batteries so that you can play on the move. It is controlled with a controller that has buttons, a D-pad and small sticks. Games come on cartridges or discs or as downloads.

The first home console was the Magnavox Odyssey from 1972, invented by Ralph Baer. At the end of the 1970s the Atari 2600 became popular in many living rooms. In the 1980s Nintendo conquered the world with the **NES** and games such as “Super Mario Bros.”. In 1989 the **Game Boy** came out, a console for playing on the move with a greenish screen. It made the game Tetris world-famous.

**Nintendo** was founded in Kyoto in Japan in 1889 and at first made playing cards. The Japanese company **Sony** brought out the first PlayStation in 1994, and the PlayStation 2 later became the best-selling console, with over 150 million units. The American company **Microsoft** joined in 2001 with the Xbox. Today the PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series X and S have been on the market since 2020. In the past there was also Sega, with Sonic the hedgehog.

Nintendo often tries to make gaming different. With the **Wii** from 2006 you control many games with movements, for example in tennis or bowling. The **Nintendo Switch** from 2017 can be used on the television and on the move because it has a built-in screen and battery. Its successor, the Nintendo Switch 2, came out in June 2025. Some consoles also have cameras or headsets for virtual reality.

Many Swiss households with children have a games console. With **parental controls** parents can decide how long and which games may be played. The PEGI age rating on the box helps with choosing. Old consoles are popular collector's items today. The Swiss Science Center Technorama and exhibitions in museums sometimes show the history and technology of video games.

begriffe.erklaerung: A games console that you connect to the television.
A small console with its own screen for playing on the move.
